title: England call up Spencer and Randall as injuries hit Wallabies prep
article_text:
Ben Spencer and Harry Randall have been named in England's squad for this month's Nations Championship after injury ruled Northampton nines Alex Mitchell and Archie McParland out of Sunday's match with Australia.

Mitchell pulled up with a hamstring issue in Saints' win over Gloucester on Saturday, while uncapped prospect McParland, 21, picked up a calf injury in last week's training camp.

McParland, who would have toured with England in July but for a severe cut to his leg in the Prem final win over Exeter, could still be in contention for England's matches against Japan and New Zealand on 14 and 21 November respectively.

Mitchell will have a scan on his hamstring on Monday to assess the extent of his injury and subsequent lay-off.

The 29-year-old has suffered three previous hamstring injuries already this year.

Leicester's Jack van Poortvliet, who started all three of England's summer Tests, seems set to continue as first-choice scrum-half.

England are facing a possible change at fly-half, with first-choice Fin Smith struggling with a calf problem and Marcus Smith and George Ford competing to deputise in his possible absence.

Elsewhere Saracens' Theo Dan has seen off competition from Nathan Jibulu, Jamie Blamire and Gabriel Oghre to secure the third hooker spot in the squad.

Dan comes in in place of Bath's Kepu Tuipulotu who, like McParland, picked up an injury during last week's three-day training camp.

Gloucester centre Seb Atkinson and Exeter wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso are also included after successfully negotiating injury comebacks for their clubs this weekend.

Midfield is the area of most selection intrigue with Gloucester's Will Joseph, who won his solitary previous cap back in 2022, and Sale's Joe Marchant, who has returned to eligibility after three seasons playing in France, included.

Bath centre pair Ollie Lawrence and Max Ojomoh, who both starred in last autumn's clean sweep, are omitted and there is no space for 20-year-old Saracens wing Noah Caluori.

After the matches against Australia, Japan and New Zealand, England will play a fourth Test against an as-yet-undecided southern hemisphere opponent in the play-off finals weekend of the new Nations Championship format.

title: Rassie Erasmus unveils established Springboks side for Italy battle in Turin
article_text:
Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus has named a familiar-looking side to take on Italy at Allianz Stadium in Turin on Saturday, featuring several experienced players in the starting lineup.

The Springboks head to Turin following their recent defeat to the Wallabies in Perth, which ended a three-Test winning streak, after beating the All Blacks 3-1 in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series.

Erasmus’ men currently sit top of the Southern Hemisphere table in the Nations Championship, with three wins from three Tests in July. The Springboks comfortably beat England 45-21, before claiming a 42-28 win over Scotland and a 43-point win over Wales.

Inspirational captain Siya Kolisi will lead the Springboks, alongside Pieter-Steph du Toit and Jasper Wiese in the back row.

It’s an experienced front row, with Malcolm Marx, Ox Nche, and Thomas Du Toit named to start, with Salmaan Moerat and Ruan Nortje in the second row.

Morne van den Berg and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu will line up in the 9-10 combination, while Erasmus has gone with the formidable combination of Jesse Kriel and Damian De Allende in the midfield.

Ethan Hooker and Kurt-Lee Arendse get the nod on the wings, with Damian Willemse returning from a recent injury to start at fullback.

The Springboks head coach said they are not underestimating Italy, who have “quality forwards and backline players”.

“Italy are a quality team who will enter this match with immense motivation with an eye on trying to start their home leg on a positive note in front of their home crowd, and they have challenged us well before, so we have no doubt they will come out passionate and driven as ever,” said Erasmus.

“They have quality forwards and backline players, and although they are missing a few key players due to injury, they have a talented squad with players who will certainly want to make their mark with the 2027 Rugby World Cup less than a year away, so they will give everything on Saturday.

“The vital factors for us, however, will be to be accurate in our execution and to play for the full 80 minutes, especially given the high stakes at the end of these three pool matches.

“Make no mistake though, they will be raring to go, not only with the Nations Cup in mind, but also to take full advantage of these matches as all the participating teams in the competition are preparing for the Rugby World Cup next year.”

The 53-year-old head coach said they have gone for a “battle-hardened” group, to continue the momentum from the July Nations Championship window, and Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry.

“We have three challenging matches ahead if we want to advance to the last game of the Finals Weekend, so our next three matches are going to be vital to lay a strong foundation for the tour.

“All our energy is focused on the match against Italy for now. Fortunately, some of the Japan-based players were able to travel to Italy earlier than the rest of the squad, so they have been working with some of the coaching staff for a few days already and are fully in the swing of things, while we had our first training session on Monday afternoon, so everyone is now on the same page.

“With the majority of the squad having played together for most of the season, we are confident that the players who participated in the Vodacom United Rugby Championship and French Top 14 will ease into things seamlessly this week at training.

“The fact that they are battle-hardened after a few tough matches will offer us a good balance with fresh players raring to go and others who come off a few challenging matches for their franchises and clubs.”

title: Rookie pair called up as injury problems mount for France
article_text:
Two more changes have been made to the French squad ahead of their Nations Championship match against Fiji, scheduled for this Saturday in Lyon.

La Rochelle’s 6’7 lock Charles Kanté Samba and Lyon’s blindside forward Antoine Deliance have joined Les Bleus to prepare for the fixture, as replacements for Anthony Jelonch and Joshua Brennan.

Jelonch and Brennan were both injured over the weekend while playing in the Top 14 for Toulouse against Pau.

Back-rower Jelonch had only been called up a week ago, as injury cover for Union Bordeaux Bègles’ Marko Gazzotti. His withdrawal backs up those, such as RugbyPass’ Gavin Mortimer, who questioned his selection in the first place, given he has barely played any rugby this season.

Former France U20 internationals Kanté Samba and Deliance are both 21 years of age and are uncapped at senior level. Both have been regulars in their respective club’s matchday 23s this season.

Since naming his original squad, head coach Fabien Galthié has seen his best-laid plans unravel. The weekend before last, after another bruising round of Top 14 action, he lost not only Gazzotti but also Fabien Brau-Boirie, Antoine Hastoy and Karl Sorin to injury.

title: Carlos Alcaraz’s chances of winning the Paris Masters in doubt after latest scheduling news
article_text:
After winning the Vienna Open, Carlos Alcaraz will now turn his attention towards winning the Paris Masters for the first time in his career.

The Spaniard does not have the best record at the Paris Masters, having never reached past the quarterfinals in his five appearances on the ATP Tour so far.

In fact, Alcaraz has only picked up five victories in his five appearances, giving him a surprisingly poor winning percentage of 50% at the indoor tournament.

While Alcaraz will still be one of the favourites to lift the title, the latest scheduling news could cause yet more havoc with the Spaniard’s chances of winning the Masters tournaments for the first time.

Having played every match possible at the Vienna Open, Alcaraz is currently scheduled to play his opening round match on Wednesday, 2nd 4th November.

That means Alcaraz will have to play five matches in five days in order to win the Paris Masters, which is not ideal to say the least.

Alcaraz might have missed a lot of tennis this year, but that would essentially boil down to 10 matches in two weeks across the Vienna Open and the Paris Masters.

The Spaniard has not been given the easiest draw in Paris, either, particularly in the early stages.

He awaits the winner of the first round match between Alex Michelsen and Jiri Lehecka after receiving a second round bye due to his ranking.

Lehecka will be the likely winner of that tie and he comes from a very impressive performance at the Swiss Indoors, where he reached the final.

Alcaraz will then likely need to beat Brandon Nakashima in the third round with Taylor Fritz or Arthur Fils potentially looming in the quarterfinals.

He has an excellent record against Fritz, but Fils could provide a very dangerous test for the Spaniard. Two of his five defeats at the Paris Masters have come against Frenchman, with Ugo Humbert and Hugo Gaston dumping Alcaraz out of the Masters event.

Alcaraz will then likely have to play Daniil Medvedev in the semifinals, which would be their second meeting in as many weeks after meeting in the final four of the Vienna Open, which was won by the Spaniard.

Alexander Zverev will likely be awaiting in the final, which means Alcaraz could have to beat three top 10 players in the same number of days.

That is definitely not ideal and a victory at the Paris Masters this year for Alcaraz could go down as one of his more impressive title victories on the ATP Tour.

title: Canterbury-Bankstown Bulldogs Announce Partnership Extension with Geely Auto Australia Through 2028
article_text:
Global automotive brand Geely Auto Australia has confirmed a two-year extension of its commercial partnership with National Rugby League (NRL) club the Canterbury-Bankstown Bulldogs, extending the relationship through the 2027 and 2028 seasons.

Under the upgraded commercial agreement, Geely will transition from its current front-of-shorts placement to secure elevated branding on the lower back of the Bulldogs’ official NRL playing jersey. The manufacturer will also maintain its designation as the Official Vehicle Partner and Official Electric Vehicle Partner of the club.

Canterbury-Bankstown Bulldogs CEO, Aaron Warburton, welcomed the expanded commercial commitment from the automotive company.

“Geely is a brand on the move, they arrived in Australia in 2025 and are already one of the fastest-growing car brands in the country, and we’re thrilled to welcome them onto our NRL jersey for 2027.

“Geely share our ambition and drive to innovate. As a global leader in their industry, they’ve backed our Club, our Members and our community, and we’re proud to take the next step together,” Warburton said.

Geely Auto Australia managing manaer, Alex Gu, highlighted the strategic value of aligning with the rugby league club’s broad community reach.

“The Geely Auto brand has grown significantly during our time in Australia, and it’s been rewarding to see our partnership with the Bulldogs evolve with us.”

“Having established a strong foundation together, this next chapter of our partnership provides an opportunity to connect with more Australians through one of the country’s most passionate communities.

“We’re proud to be on this journey together and look forward to exploring our partnership further in 2027 and beyond,” Gu said.

Geely initially entered the Australian sports sponsorship landscape in November 2025 by partnering with Canterbury-Bankstown.

The relationship has focused on interactive fan engagements and match-day activations at Accor Stadium. During the 2026 NRL season, Geely headlined the club’s Round 24 match-day activation, featuring its newly launched Geely EX2 model and awarding the electric vehicle to a registered Bulldogs member as part of a major consumer promotion.

title: McDonald’s Says Goodbye to FIFA After 32 Years: What Failed in Its Largest World Cup Campaign? - Portada-online.com
article_text:
This article has been provided by Portada’s sister publication Adtech.com

One of sports marketing’s most iconic partnerships is coming to an end. McDonald’s has chosen not to renew its World Cup sponsorship, concluding a 32-year run that turned the golden arches into an integral part of the fan experience across generations. The decision behind the McDonald’s FIFA partnership split marks a pivotal moment in modern sports advertising.

The move follows the chain’s largest-ever World Cup activation. Although the 2026 campaign reached over 110 countries and generated business growth, its performance fell short of internal benchmarks.

However, this transition does not signify a total exit from sports marketing. Instead, it highlights a major strategic shift in how McDonald’s builds cultural relevance and measures advertising return on investment.

According to reports from Adweek, the 2026 World Cup campaign was created by Wieden+Kennedy New York, representing McDonald’s single largest marketing push of the year. Publicis’ Starcom is McDonald’s media agency.

The overall strategy featured limited-edition menu items, interactive digital experiences, collectible merchandise, and high-profile ambassador partnerships with soccer legends such as David Beckham, Ronaldinho, Thierry Henry, and rising star Lamine Yamal.

In official statements, the company noted that the goal of the McDonald’s FIFA campaign was to extend the excitement beyond stadium seats—connecting matches directly to restaurant visits, mobile app engagements, and watch-party gatherings among fans.

Despite the scale of this effort, Ian Borden, Chief Financial Officer at McDonald’s, acknowledged during the Q2 2026 earnings call that while the McDonald’s FIFA campaign drove customer engagement, the overall results missed internal expectations.

This disclosure arrived during a period of slower domestic growth in the United States, though executives did not attribute the slowdown entirely to the soccer push.

💡 Key Takeaway: The activation was by no means a commercial failure, but the financial metrics failed to justify the aggressive targets established prior to the tournament.

The end of the agreement between McDonald’s and FIFA reflects a wider re-evaluation of the fast-food giant’s commercial strategy.

Based on insights from Adweek and MarketingDirecto, McDonald’s is aiming to rely less on borrowed IP—such as major global sports tournaments, entertainment franchises, and third-party cultural partnerships.

Instead, the company plans to double down on building and expanding its owned brand assets, proprietary characters, and direct customer experiences.

Morgan Flatley, Global Chief Marketing Officer at McDonald’s, emphasized that the corporation is streamlining its marketing calendar to execute fewer, higher-impact initiatives.

This pivot does not mean abandoning sports entirely. The brand will maintain selected regional partnerships, including its Formula 1 sponsorship in Latin America and its title sponsorship of France’s Ligue 1.

However, the role of these alliances is changing: rather than serving as the central pillar of global marketing, sports sponsorships will complement an internal brand identity built directly by McDonald’s.

Is Sports Sponsorship Measurement Evolving?

The McDonald’s FIFA breakup takes place in an era where sports broadcasting continues to command huge advertising investments.

An analysis by EMARKETER, referencing data from Dentsu, indicated that 77% of global Chief Marketing Officers planned to increase their spend on sports sponsorships throughout 2026.

Yet, massive global reach no longer guarantees strong commercial returns.

Today, brand marketers must connect ad exposure with concrete business metrics: incremental sales, customer acquisition, purchase frequency, profitability, and long-term brand equity.

While a sponsorship can deliver billions of impressions and trend across social platforms, it does not automatically prove to be a better investment than owned channels, retail media networks, programmatic ads, or direct-to-consumer experiences.

💡 Industry Question: How much should brands pay to partner with global events when they could invest those same dollars into assets and experiences they fully control?

For Mexico—one of the three host nations for the 2026 World Cup—the end of the McDonald’s FIFA deal holds special relevance.

The tournament unlocked major commercial opportunities for food, beverage, e-commerce, telecom, and entertainment brands seeking to capitalize on fan enthusiasm through localized promotions.

McDonald’s participated heavily across host markets with dedicated menu items and fan activations leveraging its long-standing soccer heritage.

However, its decision to walk away from global McDonald’s FIFA ties underscores that even the most recognized sports assets must justify themselves against strict business objectives.

For advertisers across Mexico and Latin America, this move reinforces the need for marketing strategies that extend beyond event visibility. Integrating first-party data, loyalty programs, digital experiences, and clear attribution models helps keep marketing campaigns profitable long after the final whistle.

Although McDonald’s did not publicly disclose the cost of its FIFA agreement or granular ROI figures, its decision brings to light a growing tension between traditional sponsorship value and owned digital ecosystem growth.

After 32 years, McDonald’s is not stepping away from sports as an ad channel. Instead, it is reassessing how much value it gets from a borrowed audience versus the direct relationships it can build and retain on its own.

title: WTA and TikTok announce global content partnership to connect the next generation of tennis fans
article_text:
The WTA (Women's Tennis Association) and TikTok on Monday announced a global content partnership to expand how fans discover and experience women’s tennis, combining player-led storytelling, creator content and innovative digital experiences to provide more ways to follow the excitement on TikTok.

The announcement builds on the successful collaboration between the WTA and TikTok over the past year, growing engagement with women’s tennis on the platform. The WTA has since surpassed one million TikTok followers, with content generating more than 250 million combined video views and engagements year to date, representing an increase of 41% year-on-year. Overall #WTA posts have seen more than a 50% increase over the last year.

On November 3, ahead of the 2026 FAGE WTA Finals in Indian Wells, TikTok will exclusively livestream the official Draw Ceremony, giving fans around the world a center court seat as the matchups are revealed. The livestream will set the stage for the season-ending championship taking place November 8–15, where fans will see the world's top eight singles players and doubles teams compete for one of the most prestigious titles in women's tennis.

Fans will also be able to discover and follow the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz through TikTok GamePlan, a dedicated sports content experience featuring tournament hubs across eligible WTA 1000 events, select WTA 500 tournaments and the WTA Finals. The hubs will bring official content together in one place for fans to explore throughout the season, designed to drive discovery and deepen fan engagement.

Player-led storytelling will remain a central focus, with the WTA and TikTok collaborating to help more athletes build their presence on the platform. WTA stars are already using TikTok to share their personalities, interests and experiences beyond competition, connecting directly with fans and helping audiences across sport, fashion, lifestyle and entertainment discover women's tennis.

“The passionate and growing women's tennis and sports community on TikTok helps fans discover athletes, celebrate big moments and bring their own perspectives to the game,” said Rollo Goldstaub, Global Head of Sport, TikTok.“Together with the WTA, we’re giving sports fans more ways to experience the Tour, from player-led storytelling and creator access to live moments and dedicated destinations with TikTok GamePlan. It’s about making the Tour part of the conversation on TikTok and giving new audiences and tennis lovers an even closer connection to the players and moments they can discover on TikTok.”

The collaboration will also support the development of the WTA Creator Club, an initiative designed to bring digital creators closer to women's tennis through unique content opportunities and access to tournaments around the world. Participating creators will capture and share the sport through unique viewpoints, offering fans an authentic look at life on Tour, from behind-the-scenes moments to the stories beyond the court.

"Women's tennis is having a real cultural moment, and our players are at the heart of it. They're not only extraordinary athletes, but global personalities who are influencing conversations far beyond sport,” said Sarah Swanson, Chief Brand Officer, WTA. “Our work with TikTok over the past year has demonstrated the growing global momentum behind women's tennis and the potential to reach and engage audiences in new ways. Building on that momentum, we’re delighted to be starting this week by livestreaming the draw ceremony at our crown jewel event, the FAGE WTA Finals. By combining the power of our players and tournaments with TikTok's creativity and reach, we’re looking forward to making women's tennis more accessible and engaging for the next generation."

title: Zverev receives World No. 1 trophy in Paris
Jodar marches past Tabilo, lays down Live Race marker in Paris
article_text:
Rafael Jodar sent an early signal to his Nitto ATP Finals qualification rivals on Monday at the Rolex Paris Masters, where he marched to an opening victory against Alejandro Tabilo.

Having defeated Chilean Tabilo for the loss of just six games in Basel last week, Jodar went one better in the French capital by posting a 6-2, 6-3 victory. The 20-year-old Jodar, who was competing on the same day he broke the Top 10 of the PIF ATP Rankings for the first time, converted five of 12 points he earned, according to Infosys ATP Stats.

Jodar is currently ninth in the PIF ATP Live Race To Turin, which is into its final week. He is just inside the cut for the Nitto ATP Finals and, with his dominant Day 1 victory in Paris, the #NextGenATP star has cranked up the pressure on those directly above and below him in the battle to qualify for the prestigious season finale in Turin.

“[I had] the same mindset and mentality I have had this first year,” Jodar said when asked about the keys to his win against Tabilo. “I tried to play my game, but every match is different and especially when you don’t know the tournament, because it’s my first year here in Paris. I’m enjoying it and am happy to get the first win.”

Jodar and Tabilo have played five times in 2026. The Chilean lefty won their first meeting for the loss of just three games in Indian Wells in March, but Jodar has since won eight of the nine sets they have contested and leads 4-1 in the pair’s Lexus ATP Head2Head series.

Up next for Jodar in Paris will be a second-round meeting with Casper Ruud, who raced past qualifier Juan Manuel Cerundolo 6-3, 6-2. Ignacio Buse was also a first-round winner in Jodar’s quarter of the draw: The Peruvian overcame Zizou Bergs 6-2, 6-4 to advance to face fourth seed Daniil Medvedev.

In the top half of the draw, Lorenzo Musetti set a blockbuster second-round clash with new World No. 1 Alexander Zverev. The former World No. 5 Musetti edged Hubert Hurkacz 7-6(3), 7-6(10) for his first Rolex Paris Masters match win since his quarter-final run in 2022.

There was also some early joy for a home favourite in Paris. Luca Van Assche defeated Mariano Navone 6-3, 7-5 to earn his first win at his home Masters 1000 event. The 22-year-old Van Assche, who broke the Top 40 for the first time in August, will take on 15th seed Learner Tien or Stefanos Tsitsipas for a third-round spot.

title: SIT brings Bengals partnership to Spain, rounding out Madrid game coverage
article_text:
With the NFL’s upcoming international game in Madrid, Spain, fast approaching, ticketing and fan engagement brand Sports Illustrated Tickets (SIT) has expanded its agreement with the Cincinnati Bengals franchise to cover the high-profile game.

The Bengals will face the Atlanta Falcons (another SIT partner) at the iconic 84,000-capacity Santiago Bernabeu stadium on November 8, with SIT to serve as the team's official fan experience partner around the game.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Through the deal, SIT will offer Bengals fans the chance to win tickets to the game through a sweepstakes competition. Furthermore, SIT will also serve as the presenting sponsor of the Bengals’ fan party activation in Madrid.

This announcement comes soon after SIT struck a similar deal with the Falcons, ensuring that it has consolidated its coverage of the NFL’s annual Spain matchup.

SIT is already experienced in the Spanish market, having served as the NFL’s fan engagement partner for its first-ever international game in Madrid in the 2025-26 season.

At that time, SIT chief executive David Lane spoke to Sportcal (GlobalData Sport), explaining: “The game may be held in Madrid, but this is a global event, and a global audience will be tuning in, so it creates increased awareness and opportunities for us as Sports Illustrated Tickets.

“The Spanish market is a focus for us, and we're in active conversations with multiple opportunities and partners there. This [partnership] just helps to start that foundation of what we think is one of the biggest opportunities we see in the world.

“With a partner like the NFL, a stadium [like the Bernabeu], and the team that's responsible for local operations, they are capable of putting on what will be a spectacular game.”

SIT is already an officially licensed NFL ticket vendor through the league’s “open” ticketing system, NFL Ticket HQ.

Recently, it also became the official fan experience partner of the NFL in the UK, in a deal spanning the recent trilogy of London international games.

Having partnered with the league in London this season, and with its partnership with the New England Patriots including the team’s game in Munich, Germany in November, this Spain partnership ensures SIT will feature at five of the six NFL international games in Europe this year.

The Bengals are one of seven NFL teams to partner with SIT, following the Patriots, Falcons, Pittsburgh Steelers, Washington Commanders, Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and most recently, the Jacksonville Jaguars.

title: Sportfive acquires 4sports Hockey to expand athlete management business
article_text:
Sportfive, the heavyweight international sports marketing agency, has agreed a deal to acquire 4sports Hockey, the Switzerland-based athlete management agency specialising in ice hockey.

The acquisition expands Sportfive’s athlete management business into international ice hockey and enhances its global athlete management offering.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Headquartered in Zug, 4sports Hockey operates internationally with offices in Switzerland, Germany, Sweden, Finland, and the United States and represents around 300 clients.

Its roots date back to 2006, with the current independent company established in 2019.

The agency combines former professional players, agents, and hockey specialists, providing representation and support to athletes across European leagues and North America’s NHL.

Its services span player representation, player development, career planning, contract negotiations, as well as off-ice and business services.

The acquisition complements Sportfive’s existing athlete management activities across golf, soccer, and tennis.

4sports Hockey founder Daniel Giger will continue to lead the business alongside Peter Forsberg, Johan Finnström, Micke Johansson, and Timo Machleid, supported by the company’s 20-member team.

Stefan Felsing, CEO of Sportfive, said: “4sports has built a strong position in international hockey based on deep expertise, trusted relationships and a highly personal approach to athlete representation.

“Bringing 4sports into Sportfive is an important step in our ambition to further grow our global athlete management business. By combining their hockey expertise and international network with Sportfive’s global reach and broader commercial capabilities, we see significant opportunities to create additional value for athletes and grow the business internationally.”

Giger added: “Joining Sportfive gives us the opportunity to build on what has made 4sports successful while significantly expanding the platform available to our athletes.

“Sportfive’s international reach, global sales organization, and relationships across the sports industry open up exciting opportunities for our business and our clients. At the same time, our commitment to personal relationships, deep hockey expertise, and putting our players first will remain at the heart of everything we do.”

title: Huddersfield Giants sign Autex Acoustics stadium naming rights deal
article_text:
Huddersfield Giants have signed a naming rights agreement with Autex Acoustics for the club’s new stadium in Dewsbury, which will be called the Autex Acoustics Arena.

The deal expands an existing relationship. Autex Acoustics has sponsored the Super League club for several years, including as a shirt sponsor. Under the new agreement, it will work with the Giants and their creative partners to develop the stadium’s branding and identity.

Autex Acoustics is part of the family-owned Autex Group, founded in New Zealand in 1967. Its UK business, headquartered in Elland, West Yorkshire, makes architectural acoustic products and supplies customers across the UK, Europe and the Middle East.

The group already has a presence in rugby league through its ownership of the New Zealand Warriors, who compete in Australia’s National Rugby League.

Simon Senior, Managing Director of Autex Acoustics UK, said, “We have built a fantastic business here in West Yorkshire over the past ten years, and although we are part of an international group, we are incredibly proud of our Yorkshire roots.

“Rugby League is also a big part of the wider Autex family through our ownership of the New Zealand Warriors, so it is great to strengthen that connection between the sport in both hemispheres.”

Ken Davy OBE, Owner of Huddersfield Giants, said, “It is incredibly important that we have the right people alongside us as we embark on this exciting new chapter. When you look around the stadium and see the developments and improvements already taking place, you can really appreciate what we are building here. Having Autex involved makes it even more special.”

title: All Blacks issue statement after member of security dies at Edinburgh hotel
article_text:
The All Blacks and New Zealand Rugby are mourning the loss of their long-time head of security, Logan Cadwallader, after a medical incident at their Edinburgh hotel.

Cadwallader had been part of the All Blacks family for over ten years and travelled with the side frequently throughout his tenure as the head of security.

All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie said the side will honour Cadwallader and the “legacy he has left on the All Blacks”.

“Logan has been a big part of the All Blacks family for a long time. He was the ultimate team man, loved and trusted by all and a true professional,” Rennie said.

“He looked after all of us, players and staff, and he was a good mate to many in this team. We are all devastated. Our thoughts are with his wife, Nannette, his children, Trey, Brooke and Mia, and his wider family and friends. As a team, we will honour Logan and the legacy he has left on the All Blacks.”

New Zealand Rugby Chief Executive Steve Lancaster extended the organisation’s deepest sympathies to Cadwallader’s family during this time.

“Logan was a valued and trusted member of the management group over the past decade, and he will be greatly missed by everyone who worked alongside him. On behalf of New Zealand Rugby, I extend our deepest sympathies to his family and friends at this very difficult time.”

NZR also recognised Cadwallader’s wide-ranging contribution to New Zealand.

“New Zealand Rugby also acknowledges Logan’s service to the country, at the highest level of the New Zealand Defence Force. Logan served in the New Zealand Army and New Zealand Special Air Service Regiment (NZSAS), with deployments to some of the world’s most demanding environments including Bosnia, East Timor, Afghanistan and the Solomon Islands. His service to his country, and the values he carried from it, were reflected in everything he did for the team.”

title: 'Women's rugby is moving at an incredible pace': PWR set for 2026/27 season
article_text:
The new league season will start on Friday 20 November when Loughborough Lightning host Trailfinders Women beneath the Friday night lights at DPD Stadium at Franklin’s Gardens.

That same weekend, Sale Sharks will host three-time champions Gloucester Hartpury, incumbent champions Saracens will host Leicester Tigers and Bristol Bears will travel to Harlequins.

It has already been confirmed that the league finale will take place at the Twickenham Stoop. Last year, Saracens claimed the title with a 52-14 win over Trailfinders Women in front of 8,009 supporters.

In the World Rugby Women’s 15s Dream Team of the Year 2026, 10 of the 15 players selected have plied their trade in the competition over the past 12 months before going on to star in Test rugby.

Genevieve Shore, JAECOO PWR Executive Chair, said: “Women’s rugby is moving at an incredible pace, and the JAECOO PWR is right at the heart of that growth. We genuinely believe we have the best women’s rugby competition in the world, and we’re determined to keep raising the bar.

“We’re not slowing down. If anything, we’re accelerating. This season is about taking everything we’ve built and making it bigger, better and more ambitious. We have the best players in the world competing in our league, all of the Red Roses, the most exciting emerging talent in the game, and clubs that are continuing to invest in making this competition truly world-class.

“There’s a real sense that the JAECOO PWR is now the undisputed destination for the very best players in women’s rugby. That’s something we should be incredibly proud of, but also something we have to keep working hard to deliver.”

Before the new domestic season, PWR has launched its new campaign. ‘The Home of Heroes’ was established following the Red Roses’ Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 campaign and has returned as the league looks to underline its credentials as the world’s best domestic competition.

This year, the league will “level up” following the arrival of numerous international stars.

Ruby Tui, Gabrielle Vernier and Tabua Tuinakauvadra, to name just three, will now call the PWR home, while there has also been movement across the clubs ahead of the latest season.

The campaign takes inspiration from arcade gaming to “celebrate the extraordinary talent, personalities and performances that make the JAECOO PWR special”.

This season will be especially important for women’s rugby, with the first-ever British & Irish Lions Women tour taking place at its conclusion. The best players from England, Ireland, Scotland and Wales are set to tour New Zealand in September 2027.

Shore said: “The first-ever British & Irish Lions women’s series in 2027 is going to be an extraordinary moment for our sport. It’s another huge milestone for women’s rugby and something that everyone involved in the game should be excited about.

“The JAECOO PWR will have a really important role to play in that journey. Our clubs are providing the environment in which the very best players can develop, compete and perform at the highest level. We want to be producing Lions, international stars and the next generation of heroes.

“What’s exciting is that we’re not talking about what women’s rugby might become any more. We’re seeing it happen in front of us. The crowds, the quality, the investment, the players and the ambition are all moving in the right direction.

“Our job is to keep pushing. We want to be recognised around the world as the best league in the world, and we want to make sure that every season gives supporters another reason to fall in love with the competition, our clubs and our athletes.”

title: Six Red Roses stars named in 2026 World Rugby Team of the Year
article_text:
Hot on the heels of Kaipo Olsen-Baker’s crowning as World Rugby Women’s 15s Player of the Year, World Rugby has confirmed its Dream Team of 2026.

On Saturday, Black Ferns back-row Olsen-Baker was handed her award following New Zealand’s 36-7 victory over France in Christchurch. Her teammate, Elinor-Plum King, was also named World Rugby Women’s 15s Breakthrough Player of the Year.

Olsen-Baker, 24, is named in the 2026 Dream Team alongside Black Ferns teammates Braxton Sorensen-McGee, Sylvia Brunt, Ayesha Leti-I’iga and Maiakawanakaulani Roos.

New Zealand’s five players in the Dream Team are surpassed only by England’s six. World Rugby Women’s 15s Player of the Year nominees Megan Jones and Zoe Harrison are included, as are Jess Breach, Maddie Feaunati, Amy Cokayne and Hannah Botterman.

Canada’s Sophie de Goede, Da Leaka Menin and Olivia Apps are also included, while Léa Champon is France’s sole representative.

15. Braxton Sorensen-McGee (New Zealand)

The World Rugby Women’s 15s Dream Team of the Year 2026 was selected by an expert panel comprising Fiona Coghlan (Ireland), Lena Corson (France), Abby Gustaitis (USA), Heather Moyse (Canada), Shannon Parry (Australia), Melodie Robinson (New Zealand) and Danielle Waterman (England).

Following a global fan vote, Pauline Bourdon Sansus’ try against England in the 2026 Guinness Women’s Six Nations has been named Women’s 15s Try of the Year.

The scrum-half’s effort was voted ahead of tries from Olivia Apps (England v Canada, 19 September), Abi Burton (England v Australia, 12 September) and Léa Champon (France v Scotland, 9 May).

Brett Robinson, World Rugby Chair, said: “Congratulations to Pauline on winning Try of the Year and to all 15 players selected in the Dream Team.

“These awards recognise the exceptional skill, creativity and outstanding performances we have seen throughout 2026, and are a fitting way to celebrate the players who have delivered so many memorable moments on the international stage.

“From established stars to exciting emerging talents, this year’s award winners reflect the incredible depth and ambition of the women’s game.

“As we bring the 2026 international window to a close, there is much to celebrate, and I congratulate all those recognised for their outstanding contributions to another fantastic year of women’s rugby.”

title: Boulter wins despite incident getting under her skin
article_text:
Katie Boulter said it was "lesson learned" as she overcame an incident that "got under my skin" to reach the last 16 of the Hong Kong Open.

The British number one was broken by Viktorija Golubic when serving for the match at 5-2 up in the second set.

During the game, Boulter complained to the umpire after a point was not replayed for an audible noise from outside causing a distraction.

An unsettled Boulter also lost her next service game before the world number 49 came through a tie-break to take a 6-2 7-6 (7-2) victory.

"It was interesting," said Boulter, who was the losing finalist at the Hong Kong Open in 2024.

"I was playing some really good tennis. I feel like I should have closed it out but a couple of things happened.

"There was a little bit of interesting judgement which got under my skin a little bit and, usually, I'm pretty good at batting it off but I was a little tired.

"It's end of season and it seemed to get to me but lesson learned, I managed to get over the line."

Boulter, who beat world number 89 Golubic in dominant fashion when reaching the semi-finals at the Japan Open last month, will play American Claire Liu in the next round.

Meanwhile, Venus Williams suffered a 17th consecutive singles defeat as she was beaten by fellow American Mary Stoiana in the first round in Hong Kong.

The 46-year-old, who is 597th in the women's rankings, lost 6-2 6-3 to 23-year-old Stoiana, who is ranked 113th.

Williams - a seven-time Grand Slam singles champion - has not won a singles match since July 2025 and relies on wildcards to play WTA tournaments.

Cameron Norrie progressed to the second round of the Paris Masters with victory over Italy's Matteo Arnaldi.

The British number two notched a 6-4 1-6 6-3 against Arnaldi, who is ranked nine places above him in 36th, in one hour and 41 minutes to secure his first ATP Tour win since August.

"I'm just trying to enjoy my tennis. It's been a difficult year for me and I don't really care any more - I just want to play, and play to win," Norrie told Sky Sports.

"I put a lot of expectation on myself to go and win, especially being a favourite [at times]. I was getting stuck a lot and I definitely want to try to change that.

"I really just want to play every point, enjoy every point, use my skills and give myself permission to let go and play to win. Be a bit more grateful to play."

Norrie, 31, was already a break up against Arnaldi when he lost his serve in the fourth game of the opening set.

However, the Briton immediately broke back before he served out to win it 6-4 in 36 minutes.

Arnaldi broke Norrie three times in the second set to level the match, but the Briton regrouped in the decider and, after securing a break to go 3-1 up, was able to hold his nerve to close out the match.

title: Carlos Alcaraz shares immediate reaction to Ben Shelton hiring Juan Carlos Ferrero as his coach
article_text:
Ben Shelton and Juan Carlos Ferrero have been confirmed to work together from the 2027 season in one of the biggest surprises of the season.

Ferrero has been teasing return to tennis since splitting with Carlos Alcaraz at the end of the 2025 season, but not many were predicting it would be with Shelton.

Alcaraz and Ferrero achieved brilliant things together in the six years they spent together, including a monumental six Grand Slam title triumphs for the Spaniard.

Ferrero will be looking to replicate that work with Shelton, who is yet to claim a Grand Slam title in his burgeoning career in the sport.

After winning the Vienna Open, Alcaraz was asked about his thoughts on his former coach signing up to one of his biggest ATP rivals.

Alcaraz responded: “If it is true I think it’s going to be a great addition to Ben’s team and I think Juanki [Juan Carlos Ferrero] is going to do great and it’s going to help him a lot to increase his level even more so I will be aware of him.”

There is just one space on the ATP Tour rankings currently splitting Alcaraz and Shelton, with the Spaniard at world No 3 and the American at world No 4.

However, there is a major chasm of ranking points between the two players, with Alcaraz currently 3350 points above his American rival.

Shelton and Alcaraz have played each other four times in the sport, with the Spaniard leading their head-to-head with three victories.

The American’s only victory against Alcaraz came at the 2026 US Open, when Shelton won a five set classic to knock the star out of the quarterfinals of the New York Grand Slam.

Shelton, meanwhile, will be hoping that Ferrero can turn him into a genuine world beater on the Grand Slam stage, as he only has one final to his name so far.

That came at the US Open this year, but he was beaten by Alexander Zverev in four sets to end his dream of becoming the first American major winner since 2003.

Elsewhere, Shelton has reached the semifinals of the Australian Open, the quarterfinals of Wimbledon, and the fourth round of Roland Garros.

Shelton will be hoping Ferrero can help the star on clay especially, as he has previously struggled on the surface more than any other.

Ferrero was a clay court specialist during his playing days and even claimed the Roland Garros title in 2003, which was the sole Grand Slam title of his career.

title: Kjær/Kjær win first World Tour title as Europe takes two titles
article_text:
Christian Faust Kjær/Rasmus Kjær have defeated reigning European champions Ben Lane/Sean Vendy for the men’s doubles title at the HYLO Open 2026, while world champions Thom Gicquel/Delphine Delrue win the mixed doubles.

Christian Faust Kjær/Rasmus Kjær saved their best for the final day in Saarbrücken. The unseeded Danes defeated England’s second seeds Ben Lane/Sean Vendy, 21-14 21-18, to claim their first World Tour title, two wins from two after their upset at the Arctic Open.

“Rasmus just told me: ‘Don’t take this for granted, because it doesn’t come that often.’ And that’s really true,” said Christian Faust Kjær. “To finally win a World Tour title means a lot.”

The mixed doubles final guaranteed a European champion, and Thom Gicquel/Delphine Delrue of France delivered. The world champions came through three games against Denmark’s Jesper Toft/Amalie Cecilie Kudsk, 19-21 22-20 21-18, a pair formed only this year who leave with the biggest result of their partnership.

“It was the goal of the week, but to do it is always special,” said Gicquel.

Line Kjaersfeldt finished runner-up in women’s singles after second seed Pusarla V Sindhu won, 21-12 21-14. Reaching her first final since the European Championships, the Dane said the week “gives a lot of confidence”.

India's Lakshya Sen defeated Indonesia's Jonatan Christie, 21-17 21-10, for the men’s singles title, and Indonesia’s Amallia Cahaya Pratiwi/Siti Fadia Silva Ramadhanti defeated top seeds Hsu Yin-Hui/Lin Jhih Yun, 21-18 21-19, in women’s doubles.

title: Youth Olympic Games: Czechia and Madagascar in medal hunt after a day of shocks in Dakar
article_text:
Australia, Kenya, Czechia and Madagascar will compete for the medals tomorrow with second seeds the USA sensationally out of contention.

The USA were beaten by Czechia and Madagascar in Pool B. The scale of the African nation’s 12-10 upset was seen in the players’ wild celebrations following their victory.

The results in Pool B also mean Spain are out of medal contention.

Pool A was also decided with one round of pool matches left to play as Australia and Kenya won their games against China and hosts Senegal.

The final pool matches - Australia face Kenya and Czechia take on Madagascar - on 3 November will determine the semi-final line-ups.

New Zealand, gold medallists in 2018, are not present to defend their title as they did not qualify for the competition. Therefore Australia are the favourites and top seeds, and recorded the most dominant result on the opening day with a 32-0 win over Senegal.

The competition began with a Pool A 12-5 match between Kenya and China with the latter's lack of discipline seeing the African nation capitalise. A yellow card was shown to Xinlei Guo after a series of penalties by China and being a player up Kenya scored through Evalyne Afande, which was the only score of the first half.

A beautiful solo effort from Michael Mmboga started the second seven minutes and another yellow card was given to China, this time for Yuyan Hu, with more repeated infringements. But Peng Songmei scored to give China a losing bonus-point.

Australia, who won gold in 2014, beat Senegal in the next match after tries from Te Rinajade Murray, Darci Mackay, Talia Berryman, Grace Buchanan and two from Mia Shelley.

Spain and Czechia got their tournaments underway with the first Pool B match seeing a tight second half make for an entertaining match. Czechia came out with the 35-17 win but both sides had standout scores; namely a wonderfully rapid try by Sofia Rodriguez and an amazing solo effort by Zuzana Svabova.

The final match of the first round of pool matches came between the USA and Madagascar. It was the closest game of the day with Sariaka Raveloarisoa scoring the winning try to see it end 12-10, the result somewhat of an upset.

After a break the pool games restarted with the hosts and Kenya locked in a scrappy and tense match as the score stood at 0-0 at half-time. Josephine Kerubo, Shaheen Sada and Afande scored to give Kenya the 19-0 win.

Australia also booked their spot in the final four with another victory, this time against China, despite a red card for Keira Callaghan. When down a player Australia struggled with three second half tries from China but Layne Prince made a huge play to seal the 21-15 win.

A close match saw Madagascar beat Spain 19-12, while Czechia overcame the USA 24-21 as the day’s action concluded.

The women’s competition will wrap up on 3 November with one more pool round followed by the placing matches and medal deciders.

title: Jack Draper Warns Money-Driven Decisions Are Putting A Generation Of Players At Risk
article_text:
Jack Draper believes certain decisions by tennis bosses, combined with the current direction men’s tennis is heading, could trigger an injury crisis among young players.

The former world No.4 has played only eight events this year due to injury, and his last competitive match was in August at the Cincinnati Open. Draper has struggled with a persistent injury in his left serving arm (bone bruising). The issue has forced him to miss all four Grand Slam events in 2026, dropping him to 157th in the rankings.

After his recent struggles, Draper confirmed he’ll approach his schedule differently in the new season. In an interviewwith Bagel magazine, the Brit hit out at the pressure young players face on the Tour when it comes to their commitments.

“I’ll definitely look after my schedule as best as possible,” he said.

“Longevity is something that I want to achieve. I want to be playing for a long time. There’s a lot of young tennis players now looking at the tour schedule and people say, “Oh, you don’t need to play every week,” but at the end of the day, young players want to be number one. And to do that, you have to play week in, week out.”

This isn’t the first time someone has spoken out about the Tour calendar. Another to do so is Carlos Alcaraz, who previously said the Tour calendar is going ‘in the wrong direction’ and is ‘pushing us (the players) too much out of the line sometimes to play a lot of tournaments.’ Alcaraz missed nearly five months of action earlier this season due to a wrist injury. Meanwhile, Jannik Sinner hasn’t played since Wimbledon due to a knee problem.

“There’s been a lot of money-making decisions in tennis, especially from higher up,” Draper continued.

“And although there’s been a lot of good stuff going on, they’re really putting a whole generation in danger, getting injured all the time.

“It’s more to do with the nature of the way the game’s going as well: slower courts, slower balls and then athletes getting better. So it’s not in a good place.”

Elaborating further on slower courts on the Tour, Draper argues that they put more strain on players than in the past because of advances in training and technology.

“Athletes are having to push their bodies more and more to cope with the demands of the level that everyone can produce,” he said.

“Especially also with the nature of how slow the courts are getting, which means you can get to those balls. Tennis now is such a physically demanding sport. And obviously with the calendar being so long, and all these things combining, it’s producing a lot more injuries.”

Draper is yet to confirm where he will begin his comeback in 2027. If he returns in January, he will not be able to use a protected ranking as players must be out of action for at least six months to be eligible.

title: Bryson DeChambeau went surprisingly deep on the loneliness he felt after winning his first major
article_text:
Bryson DeChambeau went surprisingly deep on the loneliness he felt after winning the U.S. Open

Bryson DeChambeau is hardly the first successful person to achieve the ultimate goal and wonder "what now?" immediately afterward. And he won't be the last.

He did, however, go a little deeper than that during a recent appearance on the "Figuring Out with Raj Shamani" podcast.

For DeChambeau, that ultimate goal was winning the U.S. Open, something he's now accomplished twice, first winning in 2020 at Winged Foot and again in 2024 at Pinehurst No. 2. Both were extra satisfying for the Mad Scientist because he did it his way—by overpowering two iconic venues with mammoth drives that consistently put him closer to the hole than everybody else.

But the work began long before DeChambeau's 2024 and 2020. Winning our national open, twice, was something he's worked toward his whole life.

"Your entire life, you're told that's what the goal is," DeChambeau told Shamani. "The goal is to get to this trophy. And then you realize when you hit it, you go, I gave up most of my life for this. I gave 20 years of my life to do this and I did it. Well, now what do I do?"

The weight of that thought hit particularly hard for DeChambeau, who realized he had no one close to him to celebrate with after all the dust had settled in 2024.

"I mean, I don't have a family. I don't have kids. I don't have a wife," he said. "And, you know, that's one of the things where I had the trophy right next to my bed. I'll never forget. We had a nice party. We were all having fun. And I go to bed. It's tough to sleep, by the way. Your endorphins and your adrenaline is still going.

"But you sleep for the five, six hours and you wake up and you look over and you're like, oh, I won the U.S. Open. And then right after you say that, it's like, what do I do next? I'm in bed alone. I don't have my family with me. I don't have anybody around. And it's, it's a real moment of frailty and it's not easy."

DeChambeau continued: "I don't have somebody loving on me and giving me a kiss and a kid coming up on the bed and holding my hand and all that. Is that really what I want to do for my life? Is that one legacy I want to leave to? And so it really transforms you and makes you realize what life is about.

"So it's a great thing. It's also a humbling thing and it makes you feel lonely at first. But if you can get past that loneliness, you realize what life is truly about."

Fortunately, while DeChambeau doesn't quite have a family yet, he is in a relationship with former professional hockey goaltender Mikayla Demaiter, who he was photographed with last month on Marine One alongside President Donald Trump.

title: Bryson DeChambeau reveals ‘insane’ Tiger Woods actions that he didn’t like
article_text:
Bryson DeChambeau has admitted he was not a fan of how Tiger Woods approached the game during his pomp.

Woods ushered in the modern age of golf during the early 2000s, becoming one of the most dominant players the game has ever seen.

He has over 100 career wins, including 15 majors and is arguably the greatest golfer of all time.

As well as his supreme skill, Woods showcased a level of competitiveness and single-mindedness never seen before on the course.

And DeChambeau, a two-time major champion himself, says that laser focus was what set Woods apart from his rivals.

He told the ‘Figuring Out’ podcast: “Tiger was the most intense and fierce competitor I've ever met in my entire life.

"[He had] an insane ability to just say, ‘I want to beat the living s*** out of you’ because they love it.

DeChambeau admits he isn’t necessarily a fan of the way Woods conducted himself despite admiring everything he has achieved.

He added: “They just want to absolutely beat you. That's what it is. It's a weird thing.

"I don't like that. That's not the way I approach things, but I never forget him looking at you and then looking right through you like you weren't even there. And I was taken aback.

“I'll never forget, I was in the Bahamas and we were just talking about something and some people came up to him and we were talking just like we are now, very focused and then he'd go over and look at them and just look right through them.

“Like they weren't even there and they would talk to him and he wouldn't even recognize them there. But it would make it known that he didn't even see you.

“And the reason was because for him, it was always kind of a game.

“I'm not going to speak necessarily ill on him, he was a great golfer and athlete, but to get to that level that he got to of complete and utter dominance, there was a bit of, ‘I'm going to do anything and everything to beat you’.

“So on the golf course, he would go out there with that mentality, like he wouldn't even know you're there.

“He had such an unbelievable ability to tune people out, tune things out and focus on just winning. There was no other option.

“He was not going to come back with a second place finish and that insane willpower is what made him special and different from everybody else.”

Woods last victory came at the 2019 Zozo Championship while his last competitive appearance was at the 2024 Open.

Following his well-documented injury and off-the-course issues, Woods is hoping to make his comeback soon.

Woods could play in the upcoming Hero World Challenge in early December and the PNC Championship alongside his son Charlie.

There are then heavy rumours he will return to major action at the 2027 Masters next April.

title: P.V. Sindhu to skip Korea Open and Japan Masters after Hylo Open title
article_text:
P.V. Sindhu has decided to skip the Korea Open (November 3-8) and Japan Masters (November 10-15), just a day after winning the Hylo Open Super 500 title in Saarbrucken on Sunday. The double Olympic medallist signed off on a high note, beating Denmark’s Line Hojmark Kjaersfeldt in straight games to clinch the women’s singles crown, while Lakshya Sen completed a memorable double for India by winning the men’s title.

Former world champion Sindhu, who also won the Japan Open in July and finished runner-up at the French Open last week, produced a controlled and assured display to register a commanding 21-12, 21-14 victory over eighth seed and world No. 25 Kjaersfeldt in a 39-minute final.

The Indian dictated the rallies with precise strokeplay, using her reach and court coverage to keep the Dane under pressure and seal her latest BWF World Tour title.

title: Sydney Thunder diversify sponsorship portfolio across social impact, appliances and clean energy
article_text:
Sydney Thunder have strengthened their commercial portfolio ahead of the 2026-27 Big Bash season, announcing an expanded social impact partnership with Plate It Forward, a new agreement with appliance brand Omega and the renewal of their association with clean energy provider Green.com.au.

The three deals span community engagement, consumer marketing and sustainability, reinforcing the club’s commercial presence across the Weber WBBL|12 and KFC BBL|16 competitions.

The expanded Plate It Forward partnership will see the social enterprise continue as Sydney Thunder’s official social impact partner for the next two seasons. The collaboration aims to deliver 5,000 meals to underprivileged communities across Western Sydney this season, building on the 627 meals provided last summer.

Founded in 2020, Plate It Forward addresses food insecurity while creating employment opportunities for disadvantaged communities.

Sydney Thunder General Manager, Trent Copeland, said, “We’re incredibly proud to continue our partnership with Plate It Forward. Shaun and his team have really created something special and share our passion for making a real difference in the communities we represent.

“At Thunder, we believe our impact extends well beyond the cricket field, and setting a goal of providing 5,000 meals this season is a fantastic opportunity to give back to those who need it most.”

Meanwhile, Omega has joined Sydney Thunder as their official appliance partner in a two-year agreement. The Australian brand, whose portfolio includes ovens, cooktops, dishwashers and washing machines, will feature prominently on the club’s playing shirts across both competitions.

Trent Copeland added, “We’re thrilled to partner with Omega for the next two seasons. They’re a family-focused brand and, at Thunder, family and community are at the heart of everything we do. What really appealed to us was that shared commitment to bringing people together and building strong communities. Omega has been part of Australian households for many years, and we’re proud to partner with a brand that shares so many of our values. It’s also fantastic to see Omega featured on both our WBBL and BBL playing shirts this summer, and we’re looking forward to working together to build a partnership that extends well beyond the cricket field.”

Sydney Thunder have also renewed their partnership with Green.com.au, which will continue as the club’s official energy partner. The renewable energy provider will support the club’s sustainability initiatives and retain visibility across home-match signage. Its product portfolio includes solar panels, batteries, heat pumps and electric vehicle chargers.

Copeland continued, “We’re thrilled Green.com.au are staying on as our Official Energy Partner. The inspiring work they do to help Australians make their change to clean energy is why we want to work with them. Their values align with ours, and we look forward to working together both on and off the field.”

The commercial developments arrive as Sydney Thunder’s women’s team begins its WBBL|12 campaign. The side opened its season with consecutive victories, defeating Melbourne Renegades and Brisbane Heat. The team’s next fixture is against Perth Scorchers on November 5 at Drummoyne Oval.

Thunder’s 15-player WBBL|12 squad includes Phoebe Litchfield, Heather Knight, Nadine de Klerk and Lauren Bell, with Lisa Keightley serving as head coach.

The men’s BBL|16 campaign begins on December 16 against Adelaide Strikers in Canberra. David Warner, Sam Konstas, Sam Billings, Daniel Sams, Chris Green and Lockie Ferguson are among the confirmed players, with Warner expected to lead the side. Sydney Thunder will return to ENGIE Stadium on December 19 for the Sydney Smash against Sydney Sixers, marking the club’s first major home fixture of the men’s season.

The three partnerships underline the club’s strategy of building commercial relationships that combine brand exposure with measurable community and sustainability outcomes.

title: Melbourne Storm Secures Commercial Partnership with Aussie Pet Food Brand Perfect Bowl Exclusively at Petstock
article_text:
National Rugby League (NRL) club, Melbourne Storm has announced a new commercial agreement with Australian-made and owned dog food brand Perfect Bowl, available exclusively through national pet specialty retailer Petstock.

Under the commercial agreement, Perfect Bowl will integrate into Melbourne Storm’s consumer and digital channels ahead of the 2027 NRL season.

Melbourne Storm chief commercial and customer officer Tayah Bot, welcomed Perfect Bowl to the club’s commercial partner portfolio.

“Perfect Bowl is a great fit for Melbourne Storm, particularly given the strong connection many of our members and fans have with their pets.”

Additionally, Perfect Bowl will feature across the club’s digital media network, executing targeted digital marketing campaigns and fan-engagement initiatives throughout the partnership window.

title: Liam McConnell makes Scotland case as Jamie Ritchie injury opens door
article_text:
Jamie Ritchie's departure from Edinburgh in 2024 paved the way for Liam McConnell to establish himself as a regular in Sean Everitt's side. Now, with Ritchie set to miss the Nations Championship through injury, McConnell will be hoping to seize his opportunity and make his mark on the international stage.

Ritchie was forced out of his home Glasgow debut after just 10 minutes on Friday, while Matt Fagerson has missed the last three Warriors games with a groin injury.

If Fagerson is fit for the Nations Championship opener, as expected, he will likely take the number six jersey alongside Rory Darge and Jack Dempsey in the back-row, but McConnell furthered his chances with a busy performance for Edinburgh despite defeat to Benetton on Saturday.

The 21-year-old has two caps, against USA last autumn and Fiji in the summer, and has set his sights on being involved in the biggest games.

"I definitely now want to be pushing to make more and more matchday squads for some of the bigger games as well," McConnell said.

And he feels like his game is in a good place after an encouraging start to the season with Edinburgh.

"I really wanted to get off to the season with a good start. I was aware from last year that you only get probably three or four games before they select the squad, so it's important to get off to a good start if you want to be involved. That was a big motivation for me.

“I had a few niggles and stuff last year, and I worked pretty hard over my time off to try and get on top of some of them, which I have, and I'm feeling really fit at the moment. And nothing's really bothering me, so that's nice to be able to play with no worries."

And despite being a relative novice at Test level, McConnell will hope to transfer his ability to disrupt opposition lineouts if given a chance against the All Blacks.

He has six steals in the URC so far this season, the joint-highest alongside Edinburgh colleague Glen Young and two more than their nearest rivals.

"The lineouts are a whole pack thing," said the back-row man.

"I think it's definitely a strength of mine, but it takes everyone else to be on board for me and Glen [Young] to be able to get the steals. Everyone needs to be on the same page.

"This year we've realised that we can make that a strength. So we've doubled down on that and put even more work into it."

Off the pitch, McConnell says he's also feeling increasingly at home as part of the Scotland squad.

"This is my fourth squad that I've made but I've not actually been in that much because last autumn I was just in for one week. For the Six Nations I wasn't in at all because I got injured and then in summer I was only with them for three weeks so I missed a bit of the lead-up.

"I've only been around it for four weeks in total so I'm excited to be in this one for a whole block."

title: England hand surprise call-up to former Māori All Blacks forward

title: Italy captain Michele Lamaro one of 16 stood down ahead of Springboks clash

Little surprises await Gonzalo Quesada’s side, particularly after Italy endured a difficult run of summer fixtures.

title: Juan Carlos Ferrero: Ben Shelton appoints Carlos Alcaraz's former coach - will it work?
article_text:
Ben Shelton's name rarely cropped up when Juan Carlos Ferrero - the former world number one who nurtured Carlos Alcaraz to stardom - teased he was going to coach a new player.

But there are obvious reasons why it suits both parties.

For US Open runner-up Shelton, it is an opportunity to tap into a mind that knows how to win major titles and has the inside track on the world's very best.

Ferrero started working with Alcaraz when he was 15, turning his fellow Spaniard from a "piece of spaghetti" into a seven-time Grand Slam champion.

Alcaraz is seen as the most naturally gifted player on the ATP Tour, having dominated the biggest tournaments alongside Jannik Sinner before their respective injuries this season.

Guiding world number four Shelton is a different assignment.

With explosive power and supreme athleticism, the 24-year-old American already possesses weapons which can inflict serious damage.

The left-hander has been a fixture inside the world's top 20 for the past four seasons and reached his first Grand Slam final in New York two months ago.

However, he has often fallen short against the very best.

Shelton earned the best win of his career against an undercooked Alcaraz in September's US Open quarter-finals, but could not beat new world number one Alexander Zverev in the championship match.

His New York run was underpinned by an improved backhand and better defensive skills, but not being able to execute his damaging forehand in crucial moments proved costly against Zverev.

Shelton has also suffered blips against opponents he was expected to beat, including a defeat by Swiss world number 222 Jerome Kym in Basel last week.

It acted as a reminder of the work he still has to do and the consistency he needs to find.

Ferrero, who will work alongside Shelton's father and current coach Bryan, is regarded as an astute thinker and tactician.

He demands focus and clarity from his charges so they can thrive in the most intense battles. It means he will want the fiery Shelton to play smarter - and perhaps calmer in certain moments - to maximise his weapons.

"Juan Carlos is one of the great minds in tennis," Shelton said.

"His experience of winning at the highest level and developing champions will be a huge asset to our team."

Ferrero enjoyed a stellar playing career and won the 2003 French Open, but he has become known to a younger generation as the coach who guided Alcaraz to the pinnacle of the sport.

He has largely kept away from the ATP Tour since their sudden split in December last year - but that does not mean he has kept a low profile.

The 45-year-old used his new book to further promote his reputation as a 'supercoach', but can he achieve success with someone other than Alcaraz?

Ferrero always had an eye on coming back in 2027 and held exploratory conversations with a mixture of top-20 stars and younger talents.

Some talks were more serious than others but he did not discuss terms with anyone other than Shelton, who put Ferrero top of the list when considering bringing in another coach.

The plan is for Ferrero to cover 10-12 tournaments next season, including the four Grand Slams.

The pair will begin formally working together during an off-season training block in the United States, although Ferrero will watch Shelton on site at next week's ATP Finals in Turin.

"Ben has extraordinary talent, power and character," Ferrero said.

"I'm looking forward to contributing my experience and working together with everyone to help Ben achieve his ambitions."

How Ferrero gels with Shelton's dad - a former professional player who won two ATP titles - will be key.

Ferrero previously had a six-month spell coaching Zverev, which ended after a third-round Australian Open exit in 2018.

Ferrero was hired by Zverev as an outside voice coming into a father-son coaching dynamic, but the German fired him after claiming Ferrero was "disrespectful" to his team.

Ferrero later said Zverev lacked the professionalism he expected from a top player.

Shelton, known for having a strong work ethic and insatiable will-to-win, is likely to be receptive to Ferrero's demands - as long as they do not neutralise his raw weapons.

But Rick Macci, the veteran American coach who guided the Williams sisters as teenagers, believes Ferrero will find it harder to improve Shelton's technical deficiencies.

"Shelton can win a few Slams if things break his way," Macci said.

"His backhand groundstroke and return can be technically unpredictable - at the top of the mountain the margins are razor thin.

"Ferrero can help a lot in many areas because [Shelton's] backbone is better than his backhand, but getting to number one is a different landscape to mow."

title: Ahn Se-young skips Japan Masters to focus on Korea Open and World Tour Finals
article_text:
"shuttlecock queen" Ahn Se-young (24, Samsung Life Insurance) decided not to participate in the Japan tournament after playing in front of domestic fans. The absence of world No. 1 Ahn Se-young has attracted attention in the international badminton community.

Ahn Se-young will compete in the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Korea Open (Super 500), held from Dec. 3 to 8 at Jinnam Gymnasium in Yeosu, Jeollanam-do. On the other hand, she will not participate in the Kumamoto Masters (Super 500), held in Kumamoto, Japan, from Dec. 10 to 15.

Southeast Asian badminton outlet Badminton BlaBla said on Dec. 1 (Korea time) on its official social media, "The earth shakes! Ahn Se-young will not participate in Kumamoto Japan Masters 2026."

The outlet explained that Ahn Se-young decided to skip the Japan tournament to rest after competing in the Korea Open.

Ahn Se-young competed consecutively in Super 750 tournaments in Europe, including the Denmark Open and the France Open, last month. In particular, she continued her momentum by winning her 10th title of the season at the France Open.

A packed schedule since early this year has increased the need for physical management. Ahn Se-young retired injured during the Japan Open in July, and she was also unable to compete in the China Open due to injury.

This time she plans to rest after competing in the Korea Open held domestically and prepare for the World Tour Finals in December.

The Badminton Korea Association also announced Ahn Se-young's participation in the Korea Open on its official social media on Dec. 1.

The association encouraged domestic fans' interest, saying, "A chance to see the badminton queen, Ahn Se-young, play right in front of you! Don't miss it, see you in Yeosu."

In the first round of the Korea Open women's singles, Ahn Se-young will face world No. 38 Kaloyana Nalbantova (Bulgaria). If she wins, she will meet the winner of the Karupathevan Letsana (Malaysia) and Tonlorg Saehang (Thailand) match in the round of 16.

There is a possibility she would face Gunji Riko (Japan) in the quarterfinals and Miyazaki Tomoka (Japan) or Akechi Hina (Japan) in the semifinals. In the final, a matchup with Yamaguchi Akane (Japan) can also be anticipated.

Meanwhile, there are disappointed reactions in Japan over Ahn Se-young's absence.

The Kumamoto Masters is expected to feature world-class players such as Wang Zhiyi and Chen Yufei (both China), Yamaguchi, and Miyazaki. In particular, Yamaguchi told Japanese media ahead of the tournament, "I will try to face Ahn Se-young here as well," expressing anticipation for the matchup.

However, with Ahn Se-young withdrawing, the matchup between the two players in Kumamoto was canceled.

On Japanese Yahoo! Japan and others, comments such as "Yamaguchi and Miyazaki are going to Korea, this is not right" and "When will Ahn Se-young come to this tournament again" appeared, expressing disappointment. On the other hand, some understood the physical burden from competing in European tournaments.

Not only Ahn Se-young but also Kim Ga-eun (Samsung Life Insurance) and Shim Yu-jin (Incheon International Airport) will not participate in the Kumamoto Masters. Kim Ga-eun will also miss the Korea Open due to lingering injury, and Shim Yu-jin plans to compete only through the Korea Open.

Ahn Se-young's next goal is the BWF World Tour Finals, held from Dec. 8 to 13. The season-ending event has a total prize pool of $3 million, and the women's singles winner's prize is $240,000.

Through this Korea Open, Ahn Se-young will participate in an international tournament held in Korea for the first time in about a year and two months. She plans to challenge for the title in front of domestic fans and then prepare for the season's final tournament with sufficient rest.

title: PGA Tour finds new sponsor after Good Good fallout
article_text:
Two weeks ahead of putting on an inaugural tournament in Austin, the PGA Tour has a new sponsor for the event in the wake of the Good Good fallout.

On Monday, Compliance Solutions was announced as the presenting sponsor. Compliance is an accounting and tax service provider based in Longwood, Fla., and has an existing relationship with the tour, sponsoring Korn Ferry Tour and PGA Tour Champions events.

“We are proud to have their commitment and support as we prepare to bring this new event online,” said the tour’s executive vice president Dan Glod.

The move ends a whirlwind leadup for the tournament. In October 2025, the tour announced it was partnering with Good Good, a popular YouTube influencer brand and apparel company with a sizable following among younger golfers, to host a fall event. This would coincide with Golf Channel reviving the TV show “The Big Break,” which would confer a spot in the Austin field to the winner.

However in August Good Good released a promotional video that showed a man shoving a woman to the ground in a fight over a new Callaway driver. The ad, intended as a parody of the movie “Obsession,” drew immediate, far-reaching criticism, and was further inflamed by delayed apologies that many felt lacked accountability. PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp called out the video during a press conference at the Tour Championship. “What we saw was concerning,” Rolapp said. “It is clearly not aligned with PGA Tour values.” He later added the company’s response was “a bit defensive and late.”

The PGA Tour ended Good Good’s sponsorship of the event while Golf Channel canceled its planned reboot of the “The Big Break.” Retailers including Dick’s Sporting Goods, Golf Galaxy and PGA Tour Superstore removed Good Good-Callaway merchandise from stores and their websites. After Callaway ended its partnership with Good Good, while Good Good’s top two executives were pushed out.

The Austin Championship begins next week at Omni Barton Creek Resort & Spa’s Fazio Canyons Course in Austin. It is the penultimate stop on the FedEx Cup Fall schedule, with the season wrapping up the week after in Sea Island.

title: 'Emergency Procedures' In Place For Opening DP World Tour Play-Off Event Due To Middle-East Tensions
article_text:
The DP World Tour has provided anyone involved in the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship with instructions on what to do should an emergency be declared during the tournament this week.

Ongoing tensions in the Middle East, fuelled by numerous wars across the region and a recent attack on Saudi Arabia's Riyadh International Airport, have created concerns among pros and led to some big names choosing to miss the first DP World Tour Play-Off event as a result.

There were reports several weeks ago that due to security concerns the DP World Tour was exploring Spain's Real Club De Golf Sotogrande as an alternate site.

However, the European circuit has been assured both Abu Dhabi and Dubai are safe to host events in and the fourth Rolex Series event of the year is due to begin as planned on Thursday.

But in order to ensure everyone involved remains as safe as possible, a notice - shared by putting coach Jacobo Pastor on X - was sent out prior to practice rounds starting.

Titled 'Mobile Phone Alerts & Emergency Procedures', it read: "If the UAE authorities issue a mobile phone alert to the public at any point during the week whilst on site, play will be suspended immediately, signalled by a long blast of the air horns, as per the procedure for a dangerous situation.

"Players and caddies should evacuate the course as per the evacuation plans and proceed to the clubhouse.

"Tour staff will provide updates and announcements in the clubhouse, with further information shared via the Player Portal.
