Matt Fitzpatrick and Robert MacIntyre are arguably the two biggest names opting to miss the DP World Tour Play-Offs, with the Englishman consequently passing on the chance to defend his DP World Tour Championship title.

Speaking about the DP World Tour Championship in early October, Fitzpatrick said: "It's a tournament that I love going to and obviously a tournament that I play very well at, and obviously I would be very disappointed to miss it, to be honest.

"Kind of taking it week-by-week and just sort of seeing the other side of it. I've also got my eight-week-old son to think about.”

Ultimately, both Fitzpatrick and MacIntyre made their peace with staying at home. But they're not the only ones, though, with 11 of the top-70 on the Race to Dubai rankings declining the chance to tee it up in the United Arab Emirates this month over safety concerns.

Despite a healthy chunk of notable absentees, stars such as Rory McIlroy, Jon Rahm and Tommy Fleetwood are all awaiting their tee times as they bid to claim one of the biggest titles all season.

McIlroy has famously never won in Abu Dhabi and will be desperate to change that as he hunts down a record-equalling eighth Harry Vardon Trophy - a feat which would pull him alongside the great Colin Montgomerie.

The Grand Slam winner's quest begins on Thursday as Yas Links Golf Club hosts the $9 million tournament.

title: Borthwick turned down my offer to work with England
article_text:
Decorated defence guru Shaun Edwards says his offer to work for England at next year's Rugby World Cup was turned down by head coach Steve Borthwick.

Edwards, 60, left his post with France earlier this year and, after a short-term role with England's women's side, has signed up to work with Argentina until the end of the tournament.

"I had a good chat with Steve over the phone," Edwards told Rugby Union Weekly.

"I said to Steve he can make me assistant kit man and I'll be there, I'll be ready for work.

"He was very, very honest with me and I thanked him for that.

"He said he was happy with his staff and the way things have been going, and I respected him for that."

Edwards is one of the most successful defence coaches in the game, having won three Six Nations Grand Slams during a 12-year spell with Wales and then helping restore France as a global powerhouse - with three Six Nations titles secured on that side of the Channel.

He also won two Champions Cups and four English titles during his time with Wasps, initially as a defence coach before taking on the club's top job.

Edwards, who was a hugely successful rugby league star with Wigan and Great Britain in his playing days, has long been linked with England's men's side.

Approaches were made by the Rugby Football Union to bring him into their coaching pathway in 2006 and 2008, while chief executive Bill Sweeney had informal talks with Edwards in 2021 but opted against competing with France for his services.

Borthwick's backroom set-up is already set for Australia 2027, with Richard Wigglesworth overseeing defence, supported by Byron McGuigan and Joe El-Abd.

England have endured fluctuating form over the past two years, with a 12-Test winning streak ended by Scotland in February and followed by five successive defeats.

They most recently beat Fiji and Argentina and now face Australia, Japan, New Zealand and a Nations Championship play-off on successive weekends through November.

Edwards says that his brief experience with the Red Roses was eye-opening.

He was involved in the build-up to England's win over New Zealand at Allianz Stadium, in which the hosts lagged behind on possession and territory, making only seven 22m entries compared to the Black Ferns' 15.

However, Zoe Harrison's last-play try gave the hosts a memorable 26-19 victory.

"The team made 310 tackles against New Zealand and we only conceded 19 points. That is probably the biggest stat I've ever been involved with in my whole career," said Edwards.

"Normally if you go over 250 tackles, you lose because the other teams obviously had all the ball."

Edwards added that the performance was all the more remarkable to him because of the different pre-match atmosphere around the Red Roses, compared to men's teams he has coached in the past.

"The girls are very joyous on matchday whereas, as men, we've got our heads down almost like we're going to a slaughterhouse," he added.

"I was thinking afterwards that maybe that's the way to go - be a bit more relaxed before the match."

Edwards, who was linked with the vacant Fiji job secured by South African Jake White, added he is surprised that his experience has not yet led to a head coach role with a Test side.

He believes he was a strong contender to take over the Wales job from Warren Gatland when the New Zealander ended his first stint with the country in 2019.

Wales opted instead to appoint Scarlets coach Wayne Pivac.

"I thought I might have got the Wales job when Warren decided to leave, but then I went on to something which I'd always wanted to do - which is to help France," he said.

title: Technicality could allow Christ Tshiunza play for Wales and Sale Sharks
article_text:
Sale Sharks boss Alex Sanderson admits he’s made getting his in-form flanker, Christ Tshiunza, on the plane to the World Cup in Australia next year a priority.

Tshiunza, 24, has been in superb form for the Sharks since his move from Exeter Chiefs, but in the summer was ruled ineligible to play for his country because he falls 10 caps short of the 25-cap minimum to play outside Wales.

He fell victim to a little-known loophole in the regulations, which rules him out of selection after it was deemed that he turned down reasonable offers from the Ospreys and Cardiff to pen a one-year deal with the Manchester-based outfit.

Sanderson said he has spoken to Tshiunza, who won his last of 15 caps in a 12-45 defeat to the Springboks in November 2024, about staying with the Sharks beyond the end of the season.

He says Steve Tandy can pick Tshiunza if none of the four Welsh regions can match an offer from the Sharks, which Rhys Carre and Jarrod Evans have previously profited from.

“I haven’t spoken to Steve Tandy, but we’re definitely in consultation on how we can get him back into the Wales squad and playing in the World Cup is probably top of our agenda for Chris because he’s doing some good stuff for us, isn’t he?

“He desires and wants to play in the World Cup. He wants to play for Wales. And that’s going to motivate him to whatever decision he makes moving forward, but we’ve made it quite clear and obvious: we’d love him to stay.

“The one thing that takes that out of Wales’ hands is what price range we go in at. If it’s a price range above what they’re able to match, then you can play for Wales and will get paid loads of money here.

“But it’s whether or not that price level is something we can fit into our salary cap. That’s what we’re working through right now,” Sanderson told RugbyPass.

title: Jordie could join in Barrett triple whammy exit post Rugby World Cup
article_text:
Jordie Barrett is the latest of the three All Blacks brothers to be linked with a post-2027 Rugby World Cup move to Europe, with Top 14 outfit Lyon being offered the chance to sign him.

It wouldn’t be the first time Barrett, 29, who has scored 26 tries in 86 appearances for his country, has left New Zealand after spending 2024-25 on a sabbatical in the United Rugby Championship with Leinster.

Midi Olympique reports that Barrett’s CV is on the desks of the recruitment team at the Stade de Gerland, and that initial discussions are underway about the inside centre, who can play almost anywhere across the backline.

One of the biggest threats to Lyon signing Barrett (6’5, 102kg) could be Japan’s Rugby League One, which has deep enough pockets to cause problems for French sides and is generally a more attractive move for Kiwis.

Lyon are reportedly keen to extend the contract of their Fijian superstar winger Jiuta Wainiqolo, who has scored seven tries in seven games this season and is out of contract in 2028, but they want to offer him a long-term deal.

All Blacks legend and current defence coach Tana Umaga recently said that Barrett could be remembered as one of the best players ever to have come out of the country: “I think he’ll go down as, you know, one of the best we’ve had.”

But he might not be the only member of his family on the move, with Gallagher PREM Bristol Bears linked with a move for older brothers fly-half Beauden and second-row Scott, even though they’re likely only to be able to afford one or the other.

Beauden, 35, is tipped to be their main target, with veteran USA international AJ MacGinty reaching the end of his contract next summer, and they are in the market for a replacement.

Guiding world number four Shelton is a different assignment.

With explosive power and supreme athleticism, the 24-year-old American already possesses weapons which can inflict serious damage.

The left-hander has been a fixture inside the world's top 20 for the past four seasons and reached his first Grand Slam final in New York two months ago.

However, he has often fallen short against the very best.

Shelton earned the best win of his career against an undercooked Alcaraz in September's US Open quarter-finals, but could not beat new world number one Alexander Zverev in the championship match.

His New York run was underpinned by an improved backhand and better defensive skills, but not being able to execute his damaging forehand in crucial moments proved costly against Zverev.

Shelton has also suffered blips against opponents he was expected to beat, including a defeat by Swiss world number 222 Jerome Kym in Basel last week.

It acted as a reminder of the work he still has to do and the consistency he needs to find.

Ferrero, who will work alongside Shelton's father and current coach Bryan, is regarded as an astute thinker and tactician.

He demands focus and clarity from his charges so they can thrive in the most intense battles. It means he will want the fiery Shelton to play smarter - and perhaps calmer in certain moments - to maximise his weapons.

"Juan Carlos is one of the great minds in tennis," Shelton said.

"His experience of winning at the highest level and developing champions will be a huge asset to our team."

Ferrero enjoyed a stellar playing career and won the 2003 French Open, but he has become known to a younger generation as the coach who guided Alcaraz to the pinnacle of the sport.

He has largely kept away from the ATP Tour since their sudden split in December last year - but that does not mean he has kept a low profile.

The 45-year-old used his new book to further promote his reputation as a 'supercoach', but can he achieve success with someone other than Alcaraz?

Ferrero always had an eye on coming back in 2027 and held exploratory conversations with a mixture of top-20 stars and younger talents.

Some talks were more serious than others but he did not discuss terms with anyone other than Shelton, who put Ferrero top of the list when considering bringing in another coach.

The plan is for Ferrero to cover 10-12 tournaments next season, including the four Grand Slams.

The pair will begin formally working together during an off-season training block in the United States, although Ferrero will watch Shelton on site at next week's ATP Finals in Turin.

"Ben has extraordinary talent, power and character," Ferrero said.

"I'm looking forward to contributing my experience and working together with everyone to help Ben achieve his ambitions."

How Ferrero gels with Shelton's dad - a former professional player who won two ATP titles - will be key.

Ferrero previously had a six-month spell coaching Zverev, which ended after a third-round Australian Open exit in 2018.

Ferrero was hired by Zverev as an outside voice coming into a father-son coaching dynamic, but the German fired him after claiming Ferrero was "disrespectful" to his team.

Ferrero later said Zverev lacked the professionalism he expected from a top player.

Shelton, known for having a strong work ethic and insatiable will-to-win, is likely to be receptive to Ferrero's demands - as long as they do not neutralise his raw weapons.

But Rick Macci, the veteran American coach who guided the Williams sisters as teenagers, believes Ferrero will find it harder to improve Shelton's technical deficiencies.

"Shelton can win a few Slams if things break his way," Macci said.

"His backhand groundstroke and return can be technically unpredictable - at the top of the mountain the margins are razor thin.

"Ferrero can help a lot in many areas because [Shelton's] backbone is better than his backhand, but getting to number one is a different landscape to mow."

title: Ben Shelton explains the key area of his game he wants Juan Carlos Ferrero to improve
article_text:
Ben Shelton and Juan Carlos Ferrero are set to work together from the 2027 season, after months of speculation about who the Spanish could would work with.

Many names were touted for Ferrero, with the likes of Jannik Sinner, Rafael Jodar, and even Felix Auger-Aliassime named as potentials for the Spanish coach.

However, Shelton was rarely in those conversations, so it came as somewhat of a surprise when both men confirmed the news on the 1st November.

Shelton, who is currently the world No 4 on the ATP Tour rankings, will be looking to gain Grand Slam success under Ferrero and he has explained the reasons why he opted for Carlos Alcaraz’s former coach.

Speaking to TNT Sports, he said: “A great coach, one of the best coaches in the world. Was also a world number one as a player. I think there’s so much experience and wisdom that he can bring to our team and make a big difference for me in my career.”

In a later interview with Sky Sports Tennis’ Ryan Harrison, Shelton elaborated in exactly which areas of his game he wants Ferrero to address.

“I’m super excited. I think obviously, he was a very, very elite player. Elite coach as well, he brings so much experience to my team. I think the combination between him and my dad is going to be great for me,” he explained.

“I’m excited to start working together, I think there’s a lot to learn from someone like him. I’m fully ready to lean into that in the off-season and see what we can do next year. No, I mean a million things, but I want to become a more well-rounded player.

“Obviously all court player and develop all the skills you need to be at the top of the game. I think there’s endless things that we can work on, but I also want to become a better player on all surfaces.

“I think there’s a lot of errors he can help me on in clay court tennis and help me become a better clay courter. Yeah, I’m looking forward to adding all of that.”

Before Shelton links up with Ferrero, he is set to play two more further tournaments with just his father as his main coach.

Those will be at the Paris Masters, where is awaits the winner of Cameron Norrie and Matteo Arnaldi in the second round of the tournament.

Then, Shelton will head to the ATP Finals in Turin to round off his season, where he is looking to win the year-end tournament for the first time in his career.

title: Warren returns to main tour after three-year absence
article_text:
Marc Warren is returning to the DP World Tour three years after losing his card following a battling final eight holes that secured joint-fifth place in the grand final of the second-tier HotelPlanner Tour.

The 45-year-old Scot, the oldest player in the field, started the week 20th in the Road to Mallorca rankings and needed to rise to the top 15 to qualify for the main tour next season.

He slipped to 22nd at the turn in Mallorca, Spain, but finished 13th overall after a back-nine fightback left him seven shots behind winner Julien Sale.

The Frenchman secured second place overall behind Hamish Brown, the Danish-born son of a former Scottish club professional, with English pair John Gough and Will Enefer in 10th and 12th respectively.

Warren, who has four wins on the main tour and a highest ranking of 48 in the world, told the Scotsman: "I had a look at the leaderboard and thought I needed that putt on 18.

"I had to make a birdie. There was no playing safe at that stage for me. I knew we had to make three on 18. That meant three good shots were required and that's what we got.

"To see it drop in was great and to see the smiles on the faces of family and friends makes it all worthwhile.

"We kind of said yesterday that there might be a point where you have to put the foot down a little bit."

Sale's four-stroke win means the 29-year-old steps up to the main tour for the first time, while Brown held on to second place to secure the season-long title.

The 27-year-old Brown, who qualified for the main tour for the first time in 2024, was born in Aalborg, with father Marcus having moved from Perthshire to Denmark to become a club professional in 1985.

Brown said: "It means a lot. It gives me a lot of confidence.

"I had a tough year last year on the DP World Tour, but I thought I wasn't too far away. It's just moments throughout a season that need to go your way and I'm not scared of it for next year.

"I'm quite looking forward to it because I know what it is now.

"It's been a proper grind again today. Ultimately, I couldn't win today thanks to a good Frenchman, who played extremely well."

title: Perfect Game Media Rights Partnership Adds Minority Prospects as Third Creator Platform of 2026

- Under the new agreement, select Perfect Game events will air on Minority Prospects TV, YouTube and Instagram, with both sides sharing content and promotion.

- This is Perfect Game’s third creator-native media rights deal in 2026, following Youth Prospects in April and Doubted Athletes in June.

- The partnership went live in October at the WWBA World Championship in Jupiter, Florida, Perfect Game’s top fall event.

Perfect Game, which describes itself as the world’s largest youth baseball and softball platform and scouting service, announced a media rights partnership with Minority Prospects on November 2, 2026. Under the deal, the Atlanta-based organization will broadcast select Perfect Game events across its social channels. According to Perfect Game, it is the company’s third media rights partnership with a creator-native platform this year.

The agreement gives Minority Prospects rights to carry select Perfect Game events on all of its social media platforms, including Minority Prospects TV, its YouTube channel and its Instagram account, according to the release. The two organizations will also collaborate on content and cross-promotion.

The release did not specify which events are included or disclose financial terms.

The partnership launched before the announcement. Minority Prospects produced content last month at the WWBA World Championship in Jupiter, Florida, which Perfect Game calls its premier fall event. Coverage featured top amateur players competing in front of college coaches, professional scouts and former MLB players, the company said.

Perfect Game said the deal gives it another channel to reach players, families and fans. For Minority Prospects, the release says the partnership gives its athletes and audiences greater access to the largest events in amateur baseball.

“Launching this partnership in Jupiter, in front of the best players and evaluators in the country, was the right way to start, and we’re excited about what we can build together,” said Perfect Game CEO Rob Ponger.

Alexander Wyche founded Minority Prospects in Atlanta in 2020. The release describes it as the largest platform in the world for minority baseball and softball prospects. Its track record in six years, as cited in the release:

The organization’s nonprofit arm, MBP Helping Hands, runs those clinics alongside educational and community outreach programs.

Minority Prospects also operates its own national event calendar. That calendar includes the HBCU All-Star Games, the MBP All-American Game presented by Adidas, the MBP Collegiate League and the MBP Junior World Series.

“Together, we can expand opportunities, increase exposure and help ensure that talent, not access, determines a young athlete’s future,” said Wyche, who serves as CEO and founder.

Perfect Game says it produces nearly 10,000 events each year, spanning hundreds of thousands of games and showcases nationwide. The scale of that event footprint is why its inventory carries weight in scouting circles.

- More than 2,600 players who appeared in a Perfect Game event have reached Major League Baseball.

- Since 2003, 16,397 Perfect Game alumni have been selected in the MLB First-Year Amateur Player Draft.

- In the 2025 Draft, 92 percent of all selected players had played in Perfect Game events, and every first-day pick had attended one.

The new deal pairs that event volume with a distribution partner that has built its audience on social video. Perfect Game owns the events. Minority Prospects brings the channels and the community following.

The Minority Prospects agreement follows two earlier 2026 deals: Youth Prospects signed in April and Doubted Athletes signed in June. Perfect Game frames all three as a way to meet players, families and fans where they already are, through platforms with established amateur baseball and softball audiences.

The pattern is consistent across the three. Perfect Game is licensing coverage of its events to digital-first media brands rather than keeping that coverage in-house. Each partner brings its own audience.

The deals so far have shared a structure but left key details unannounced. Perfect Game has not said how coverage of a given event is divided when more than one creator partner wants it, or whether more partners will be added before the 2027 season.

title: Defending champs TKR secure boost for CPL as bpTT steps up
article_text:
Five-time champions and defending titleholders Trinbago Knight Riders (TKR) have secured major backing for the upcoming Republic Bank Caribbean Premier League (CPL) season, officially locking in bp Trinidad and Tobago (bpTT) as a key sponsor.

The historic partnership was sealed on Tuesday at a signing ceremony at the Hyatt Regency, Port-of-Spain, marking the energy giant’s first-ever national-level sports sponsorship of this scale.

TKR enter the 2026 campaign riding high as the CPL's most successful franchise, aiming to add a sixth star to their chest. The alliance with bpTT brings powerful local backing to the team as they prepare to battle the region’s best on cricket’s biggest regional stage.

"bpTT is committed to supporting sport, culture and national pride in T&T," said David Campbell, President of bp Latin America and the Caribbean. "We are honoured to come on board as a sponsor of the Trinbago Knight Riders. TKR’s success is based on dedication and a commitment to excellence–qualities that align to our values at bp. We are looking forward to accompanying TKR on their journey to defend their CPL title."

For bpTT, the deal marks a bold expansion of its sports investment strategy. The sponsorship builds on bpTT’s long-standing support for sport, particularly in their fenceline community of Mayaro and Guayaguayare, and represents an expansion of that commitment to a wider national platform.

Coinciding with bpTT’s 65th anniversary of operations in Trinidad and Tobago, company representatives noted that partnering with TKR reflects six and a half decades of shared values, passion, and national pride.

With the 2026 CPL season fast approaching, the defending champions now have the backing of one of the country's biggest corporate giants as they set their sights on back-to-back glory.

title: Shaun Edwards: England turned down my offer to join coaching staff
article_text:
Decorated defence guru Shaun Edwards says his offer to work for England at next year's Rugby World Cup was turned down by head coach Steve Borthwick.

Edwards, 60, left his post with France earlier this year and, after a short-term role with England's women's side, has signed up to work with Argentina until the end of the tournament.

"I had a good chat with Steve over the phone," Edwards told Rugby Union Weekly.

"I said to Steve he can make me assistant kit man and I'll be there, I'll be ready for work.

"He was very, very honest with me and I thanked him for that.

"He said he was happy with his staff and the way things have been going, and I respected him for that."

Edwards is one of the most successful defence coaches in the game, having won three Six Nations Grand Slams during a 12-year spell with Wales and then helping restore France as a global powerhouse - with three Six Nations titles secured on that side of the Channel.

He also won two Champions Cups and four English titles during his time with Wasps, initially as a defence coach before taking on the club's top job.

Edwards, who was a hugely successful rugby league star with Wigan and Great Britain in his playing days, has long been linked with England's men's side.

Approaches were made by the Rugby Football Union to bring him into their coaching pathway in 2006 and 2008, while chief executive Bill Sweeney had informal talks with Edwards in 2021 but opted against competing with France for his services.

Borthwick's backroom set-up is already set for Australia 2027, with Richard Wigglesworth overseeing defence, supported by Byron McGuigan and Joe El-Abd.

England have endured fluctuating form over the past two years, with a 12-Test winning streak ended by Scotland in February and followed by five successive defeats.

They most recently beat Fiji and Argentina and now face Australia, Japan, New Zealand and a Nations Championship play-off on successive weekends through November.

Edwards says that his brief experience with the Red Roses was eye-opening.

He was involved in the build-up to England's win over New Zealand at Allianz Stadium, in which the hosts lagged behind on possession and territory, making only seven 22m entries compared to the Black Ferns' 15.

However, Zoe Harrison's last-play try gave the hosts a memorable 26-19 victory.

"The team made 310 tackles against New Zealand and we only conceded 19 points. That is probably the biggest stat I've ever been involved with in my whole career," said Edwards.

"Normally if you go over 250 tackles, you lose because the other teams obviously had all the ball."

Edwards added that the performance was all the more remarkable to him because of the different pre-match atmosphere around the Red Roses, compared to men's teams he has coached in the past.

"The girls are very joyous on matchday whereas, as men, we've got our heads down almost like we're going to a slaughterhouse," he added.

"I was thinking afterwards that maybe that's the way to go - be a bit more relaxed before the match."

Edwards, who was linked with the vacant Fiji job secured by South African Jake White, added he is surprised that his experience has not yet led to a head coach role with a Test side.

He believes he was a strong contender to take over the Wales job from Warren Gatland when the New Zealander ended his first stint with the country in 2019.

Wales opted instead to appoint Scarlets coach Wayne Pivac.

"I thought I might have got the Wales job when Warren decided to leave, but then I went on to something which I'd always wanted to do - which is to help France," he said.

title: Tennis, ATP – Rolex Paris Masters 2026: Buse downs Bergs
article_text:
The Belgian, ranked No. 40, made 29 unforced errors and lost 6-2, 6-4, unable to repeat his Shanghai win. Ignacio Buse, 22, is the first Peruvian to win a match at the event and faces fourth seed Daniil Medvedev next.

Zizou Bergs could not repeat his Shanghai win over Ignacio Buse. The Belgian, ranked No. 40, lost 6-2, 6-4 in 1 hour 20 minutes in the first round of the Paris Masters 1000 on Monday, as Buse became the first Peruvian to win a match at the event and set up a meeting with fourth seed Daniil Medvedev.

Bergs hit 23 winners to Buse’s 12, but made 29 unforced errors, 17 of them in the first set. The Peruvian made 11, converted four of his 10 break points and dropped serve only once, in the second set.

The result reversed their only previous meeting, in Shanghai this season, when Bergs won 6-0, 6-3. Bergs, who won the Eastbourne title this season, had reached the second round in Paris in each of the past two years.

Buse, 22, ranked No. 33 and playing the event for the first time, earned his first Masters 1000 win on hard courts. He had lost his four previous matches at that level on the surface. He has won two titles this season, in Hamburg and Winston-Salem, and came into the Rolex Paris Masters with a 24-21 record in 2026.

Medvedev, who received a first-round bye, won the title in 2020 and has a 12-7 record at the event. He has won four titles this season and has already qualified for the Nitto ATP Finals in Turin.

title: “The Masters 1000 with the best atmosphere”: Van Assche beats Navone for first Paris win
article_text:
The Frenchman, ranked No. 47, beat Mariano Navone 6-3, 7-5 without dropping serve for his first win in Paris and a personal-best 13th of the season. Stefanos Tsitsipas or 15th seed Learner Tien await in the second round.

Frenchman Luca Van Assche saved all three break points he faced and held all 10 of his service games to beat Argentinian Mariano Navone 6-3, 7-5 in 1 hour 55 minutes in the first round of the Paris Masters 1000 on Monday. He was the first of the four Frenchmen in action on Monday to reach the second round, where he will face Stefanos Tsitsipas or 15th seed Learner Tien, who play on Tuesday in Alexander Zverev’s quarter.

The 22-year-old, ranked No. 47, earned his first win at the event at his second attempt, after a first-round exit in 2023. It was his 13th win of the season, a personal best, and the third Masters 1000 win of his career.

“A lot of pleasure, a lot of joy to have won this first match here in Paris,” Van Assche said in French. “Playing in France and winning matches always feels extremely good.”

Van Assche won the only ATP title of his career in Estoril in July, beating Alexander Blockx 6-4, 4-6, 7-5 in the final.

Van Assche broke Navone in the opening game and saved two break points at 3-2. He broke again at 5-3 to take the set on his first set point.

He saved another break point in the opening game of the second set, which then went with serve until 6-5, when Van Assche broke on his first match point. He won 86% of the points behind his first serve and hit seven aces, while Navone made 28 unforced errors to his 20.

Navone, ranked No. 48, won the Bucharest title in March, beating Daniel Merida 6-2, 4-6, 7-5 in the final, and lost the Geneva final to Learner Tien 3-6, 6-3, 7-5 in May.

Van Assche grew up in Paris and watched matches at the tournament as a child. “I really think it’s the Masters 1000 with the best atmosphere,” he said.

title: Mixed Fortunes For LIV Players At Second Stage Of DP World Tour Q-School As Final-Stage Field Confirmed
article_text:
The battle to secure DP World Tour cards for the 2026 season is well underway.

A week ago, at the Genesis Championship, several players earned their cards via the season-long Race to Dubai rankings.

Then, at the HotelPlanner Tour Grand Final, more cards were claimed, with the top 15 in the Race to Mallorca rankings all securing their places on the circuit for 2027.

There are more cards on the line at DP World Tour Q-School, too, although we will need to wait until next week to see who earns their card via that route.

The Final Stage will be held between November 6th and November 11th at Infinitum Golf in Spain, where the top 15 players and ties after six grueling rounds will claim spots on the DP World Tour for the 2027 season.

Players have been competing across four venues in Spain during this week’s Second Stage, with a number of notable names - including some LIV golfers - among them.

In total, 80 players have booked their places in the Final Stage.

One of the venues was Desert Springs Golf Club in Almería, where 20 places in the Final Stage of Q-School were up for grabs.

Michael La Sasso, who won LIV Golf Indianapolis, was in the 80-player field - although he won’t be going any further after finishing at five-under par and tied for 65th.

LIV Golf wildcard Yosuke Asaji got closer, but he suffered the same fate, exiting Q-School after placing T26th at 12-under-par.

Three-time Asian Development Tour winner Ahmad Baig, of Pakistan, finished top of the leaderboard at Desert Springs, with others safely into the Final Stage including runners-up Jack Yule and former LIV Golfer Kieran Vincent.

The tournament at Golf Las Pinaillas in Albacete offered 19 places in the Final Stage, with a six-man playoff required to settle the final four spots.

Spaniard Albert Boneta finished top of the leaderboard at 19-under, so the playoff was of no concern to him, but four players ended on 12-under after four rounds.

In the end, Sweden's Bjorn Akesson and the former LIV player Luis Masaveu were the two to miss out via extra holes while Yuvraj Sandhu, Jack Buchanan, Alexandre Vandermoten and David Lundgren all made it through.

One notable player in the field was Michael Stewart of Scotland, who made headlines by almost doubling his 15-year career earnings with a T4 at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship in just his fifth DP World Tour start.

However, he could only finish T46th in Spain to miss out on the Final Stage.

Former LIV Golfer and two-time DP World Tour winner Justin Harding was another to fall short, placing T40th at seven-under-par.

Ex-Florida Gators star Fred Biondi, who made the tough decision to miss the 2023 US Open and the 2024 Masters to turn pro, also failed to make it the Final Stage after he finished T36th.

At Isla Canela Links in Huelva, Dutch pro Ji Jerry led the way as 20 players progressed.

Other notable names to qualify for the Final Stage include DP World Tour winner Adri Arnaus and LIV Golf reserve Luis Carrera.

Sam Horsfield, who had been a long-time teammate of Lee Westwood and Ian Poulter on LIV Golf’s Majesticks GC, failed to reach the Final Stage after placing T52nd.

The fourth Second Stage qualifier came from Fontanals Golf Club in Girona.

There, Australian pro Anthony Quayle finished on 18 under to win by two shots.

Another to book his place in the Final Stage was 2025 Latin American Amateur champion Mateo Pulcini, who finished T4th. The younger brother of PGA Tour pro Max Greyserman, Dean, placed T12th to reach the Final Stage, too.

Two-time DP World Tour winner Shubhankar Sharma was one of the notable names to miss out, finishing T54th.

There was also a playoff at Fontanals, but only between the two players on seven-under. In the end, it was American Evan Knight who bested England's Giles Evans to snatch the last of 21 places at Final Stage.

title: Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship: Five things to know - Articles - Rolex Series

The DP World Tour season draws towards a close with its penultimate event as the Rolex Series returns at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship. Here are your five things to know.

After 40 events spanning five Global Swings, the Back 9, four Majors. three Rolex Series events and 16 national opens, the DP World Tour Play-Offs are upon us. The top 70 available players from the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World tee it up this week at Yas Links before the top 50 then move on to the season-finale at the DP World Tour Championship. Both those events form part of the Rolex Series, with Patrick Reed, Tom Kim and JJ Spaun having already been crowned Rolex Series champions in 2026. Reed's victory at the Hero Dubai Desert Classic helped him to win the International Swing and he is joined by fellow Swing winners Jayden Schaper, Mikael Lindberg, Eugenio Chacarra and Scott Jamieson in the field this week.

With the battle to keep full playing privileges on the DP World Tour having ended with the regular seaon, focus now turns to the quest to be Europe's Number One and lift the Harry Vardon Trophy. Rory McIlroy is looking to equal Colin Montgomerie's record of eight season-long wins with his fifth in a row but the Northern Irishman is in the unusual position of being the hunter rather then the hunted. With three victories this season, it is Chacarra who tops the Rankings ahead of long-time leader Patrick Reed, who has two wins of his own. Then comes Masters champion McIlroy ahead of another two-time 2026 winner in Casey Jarvis, who is the other player who could end this week on top of the Rankings with enhanced points on offer. Those enhanced points mean also mean that the jostling for dual membership with the PGA Tour is far from over, with Joe Dean currently holding the final spot. It truly is All to Play For.

Last year, Aaron Rai beat fellow Englishman Tommy Fleetwood in a play-off to win his second Rolex Series title at Yas Links, five years on from his first at the Scottish Open. It was a third DP World Tour title for Rai, who has since taken his career to new heights by becoming a Major Champion with victory at the US PGA Championship at Aronimink Golf Club in May. By doing so, he became the first Englishman in 107 years to lift the Wanamaker Trophy. That triumph, combined with a 48th-place finish at the Masters, a tied-11th finish at the U.S. Open and a tied-79th finish at The Open, saw him claim the inaugural Rory McIlroy Award, presented to the DP World Tour member who cumulatively earns the most Race to Dubai points across the four Major Championships. This week will see the 31-year-old, who is 17th in the Official World Golf Ranking, make his 27th Rolex Series appearance and fifth at this event. “Winning at Yas Links last year was a really special moment for me, so I’m really looking forward to going back and defending the title. It is a tournament that has a lot of history and a golf course that I really enjoy,” said Rai. "I always enjoy practising and playing in Abu Dhabi and fortunately, through playing well to date, I’m looking forward to finishing the year on the Race to Dubai."

The leading 70 available players on the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World tee it up in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates. Rai is among six Major winners in the elite international field, alongside Reed, McIlroy, Jon Rahm, Adam Scott and Francesco Molinari. Chacarra is the sole three-time winner this season, and he will hope to add a Rolex Series title to his CV. There are 14 players making their tournament debuts, including event winners on the 2026 Race to Dubai in David Puig, Kota Kaneko, Yuto Katsuragawa, Stefano Mazzoli, Michael Hollick, Yurav Premlall and Jordan Gumberg. There are four Qualifying School graduates hoping to impress, with Davis Bryant joined by Daniel Rodrigues, Nathan Kimsey and Gregorio De Leo, who is the sole player making his Rolex Series debut. His Italian counterparts Mazzoli and Filippo Celli qualified as graduates of the HotelPlanner Tour's Class of 2025.

The 21st edition of this event sees it take a new identity as Aldar, the Abu Dhabi-based real estate development, investment and asset management company, becomes Title Partner. This marks the next chapter in the existing relationship between the DP World Tour and Aldar, who became an Official Marketing Partner and Official Real Estate Partner of the DP World Tour in 2025. As the owner of Yas Links, Aldar is no stranger to the Abu Dhabi Championship, a tournament that has been hosted at the stunning links course on Yas Island since 2022. Aldar is the developer of the most iconic destinations in Abu Dhabi, including Yas Island and Saadiyat Island, having delivered over 35,000 homes since inception, with a growing residential development footprint in Dubai, Ras Al Khaimah, Egypt and the UK. Aldar also owns and manages a diverse portfolio of recurring income assets valued at more than USD 15 billion, which includes hotels, golf courses, shopping malls, hotels, offices, schools, and warehousing.

On the pitch and on the grid, Ukraine is not waiting for the war to end and is asking the world to invest in it
article_text:
This season, Shakhtar face some of the biggest names in European football. We have already beaten AEK Athens 3-1 at Stamford Bridge, the first win by a Ukrainian club on English soil. Sporting and Fenerbahçe fixtures are still to come in London, and Real Madrid in January.

We do it with the youngest squad in the Champions League, and under conditions no other club in the competition faces. The night before we set off for London, air raid sirens halted our league game in Rivne and sent our players into the stadium shelter. Days later, they walked out at Stamford Bridge.

Our players know they are playing not just for Shakhtar, but for people in Ukraine who finish work, switch on the game and, for a couple of hours, think about something other than the war.

But this is the fifth winter in which Russia has deliberately targeted Ukraine’s energy system. Power stations, substations and grids are struck again and again, leaving homes, hospitals and schools without power. For many families, whether they can watch us at all depends on whether the electricity and heating hold.

That is where our partner DTEK comes in. Like Shakhtar, DTEK is part of the SCM family founded by Rinat Akhmetov, and each of us supports Ukraine in our own way. While we play to bring pride to our fans back home, DTEK’s crews go back out after every missile and drone strike to get the power back on.

Everyone at Shakhtar, and our players above all, want to thank their crews and all its workers for their efforts and their sacrifices. In Ukraine, our fortunes are tied together, and we are proud to stand alongside them.

Shakhtar’s players want to thank our energy crews, and I know the feeling runs both ways. Like Shakhtar, DTEK has its roots in Donetsk, and the club’s name means “miner”. For many of our colleagues, following Shakhtar is a lifelong tradition, passed down through families who worked in the mines and power plants of the Donbas. Seeing DTEK on the club’s sleeve at Stamford Bridge carries a special meaning for them.

I have seen first hand the extraordinary commitment of our people who keep electricity flowing under constant attack. Last year alone, Russia carried out around 4,500 attacks on Ukraine’s energy system. Over four winters, our thermal power plants have been hit again and again, and 484 of our colleagues have been killed, either at work or defending their country.

Yet our crews continue to show up, often repairing the same facilities again and again. Since 2022, the crews have restored power to Ukrainian homes more than 56 million times, often knowing the next strike could come before the repair is finished.

Their determination has also changed how we think about the future of our energy system. One of the most important lessons from this war is that no energy infrastructure can be made completely safe from attack. Physical protection remains essential, but we also need to build a system that can withstand damage and recover quickly.

That means moving towards a more decentralised energy system with multiple sources of power spread across the country, making it much harder to knock out. Automation and smart grids also play an important role, helping to isolate damage and restore electricity to unaffected customers more quickly.

We are already putting these lessons into practice. Even during the war, we have built Eastern Europe’s largest wind farm and Ukraine’s largest battery storage systems. I believe these experiences offer valuable lessons for the rest of Europe.

Ukraine has gained experience that no country would wish to have, but it is knowledge worth sharing. This is also why our connection with Shakhtar means so much. The club has continued to represent Ukraine on the European stage despite being forced from its home in Donetsk more than a decade ago. Its players carry the hopes of millions of Ukrainians, including many of the people working to keep our energy system running.

Football and energy may seem like different worlds, but I see something familiar in Shakhtar’s determination to keep competing. Our teams face their own challenges every day and they know that millions of people are counting on them.

Shakhtar gives Ukrainians a reason to switch on their television this winter. Our job is to make sure that, when they do, the power is there.

Empower Sports is a global PR Agency that builds and boosts the brand of clubs, executives, coaches and athletes.

title: The World Tour heads to Asia after four exciting weeks in Europe
article_text:
After four exciting weeks of world-class badminton in Europe, the BWF World Tour now heads back to Asia, with the YEOSU VICTOR Korea Open 2026 getting underway tomorrow, 3 November.

The European leg has delivered plenty of success for European players. Anders Antonsen and Mia Blichfeldt secured a Danish double at the Arctic Open, before Alex Lanier claimed the Denmark Open title. Christo Popov then triumphed on home soil at the French Open, while Christian Faust Kjær/Rasmus Kjær and Thom Gicquel/Delphine Delrue rounded off the four weeks with titles at the HYLO Open.

Now, attention turns to Yeosu, South Korea, where several European top starts will not be compeeting, but still with some European athlethes who will look to make their mark at the Super 500 tournament, taking place from 3–8 November.

Belgium's Julien Carraggi is the only european player participating in Korea, he opens his men's singles campaign against Wang Tzu Wei of Chinese Taipei.

In women's singles, Bulgaria's Kaloyana Nalbantova faces arguably the toughest possible opening match, taking on home favourite and top seed An Se Young.

Ukraine's Polina Buhrova also features in the women's singles draw, where she will face Korea's Park Ga Eun in the opening round.

In men's doubles, Czech brothers Jiří Král/Ondřej Král face a major challenge against top seeds Kim Won Ho/Seo Seung Jae of Korea.

Bulgaria's Gabriela Stoeva/Stefani Stoeva enter the women's doubles competition as third seeds, but have been moved up as the top pair in the draw. They receive a first-round bye, advancing directly to the Round of 16.

Ukraine's Polina Buhrova/Yevheniia Kantemyr will meet Korea's Kim Hye Jeong/Lee Yeon Woo.

In mixed doubles, Gabriela Stoeva will also feature, here with partner Evgeni Panev, they will face Malaysia's Hoo Pang Ron/Lai Pei Jing, while Calvin Devereux/Desiree Toepffer from Germany will face Korea's eighth seeds Kim Jae Hyeon/Jang Ha Jeong.

The tournament features several international stars, led by home favourite An Se Young, who is listed as the top seed in women's singles. Her everlasting rival Akane Yamaguchi is seeded second.

Chinese Taipei's Chou Tien Chen leads the men's singles draw.

Korea's Kim Won Ho/Seo Seung Jae headline men's doubles, while China's Jiang Zhen Bang/Wei Ya Xin are top seeds in mixed doubles.

With strong international competition across all disciplines, an exciting week of badminton awaits in Yeosu.

title: Petition Filed to Compel Disclosure of Bayern Munich-Ajax Match Sponsorship Deals
article_text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 2 – Six Kenyans have moved to the High Court seeking orders to prevent the government from committing public funds or resources towards the planned international football friendly between German side FC Bayern Munich and Dutch club AFC Ajax at the Raila Odinga International Stadium, popularly known as Talanta Stadium.

The petitioners, led by Erick Mankuyu, want the court to compel the government to disclose the full financial arrangements for the match, which is scheduled for January 5, 2027, as part of the official opening of the newly constructed stadium in Nairobi.

The petition challenges the transparency of the event’s financing, arguing that the government has not adequately disclosed the sponsorship agreements, contractual obligations and possible public financial commitments associated with the high-profile fixture.

President William Ruto announced the planned match last week, saying it would be delivered through corporate partnerships and a self-sustaining commercial model.

However, the petitioners argue that assurances of private-sector financing are insufficient without full disclosure of the agreements and the extent of any government involvement.

The petitioners say the reported costs raise questions about who will ultimately meet the financial obligations and whether taxpayers could be exposed to direct or indirect expenditure.

The petition has been filed by Erick Sayialel Mankuyu, Julius Kimani Kamau, Dickson Kimathi Muli, Nicholas Ochieng Oyoo, Mulinge Muteti and Collins Otieno.

They have sued the Attorney General, the Cabinet Secretary for Sports, the Cabinet Secretary for the National Treasury and Sports Kenya.

The Law Society of Kenya (LSK) and Katiba Institute have been named as interested parties.

The petitioners argue that the government has a constitutional obligation to ensure transparency and accountability in the management of public resources, particularly where public institutions, facilities or personnel may be deployed for an event.

They contend that without disclosure of the financial arrangements, it is difficult for the public to establish whether the match is genuinely being financed through private commercial partnerships or whether public funds and resources will be required.

The petitioners are seeking conservatory orders restraining the respondents from authorising, allocating, releasing, committing or spending public funds towards the match unless compliance with constitutional and public finance requirements is demonstrated.

They also want the court to restrict the deployment of public resources, including security personnel, transport and stadium facilities, towards the event pending full disclosure and compliance with the law.

In addition, they are seeking orders requiring the preservation of all records relating to the match, including financial documents, procurement records, sponsorship agreements and official correspondence.

The petitioners want the respondents compelled to disclose within seven days the complete sponsorship agreements and contracts involving FC Bayern Munich and AFC Ajax, the identities of corporate sponsors and the exact financial contributions or obligations undertaken by each and detailed budgets covering appearance fees, travel, accommodation, security, insurance and other logistical expenses.

They are also seeking to know whether public funds, government guarantees, subsidies or public personnel will be committed to the event.

They are further seeking an independent audit of all public expenditure and financial commitments connected to the fixture.

The petitioners argue that disclosure is necessary to establish the extent of the government’s financial exposure and ensure that any use of public resources complies with the law.

The case is anchored on several provisions of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010, including Article 35, which guarantees the right of access to information held by the State.

The petitioners also rely on Article 201, which sets out the principles of public finance, including openness, accountability, prudent use of public money and clear fiscal reporting.

Articles 206 and 226, which provide safeguards on the withdrawal, management and accountability of public funds, also form part of the legal basis of the petition.

The petition further invokes Articles 22 and 23, which provide for the enforcement of fundamental rights and freedoms through the courts.

The petitioners have also cited the Public Finance Management Act, 2012, and the Access to Information Act, 2016, in seeking disclosure of the financial and contractual arrangements.

They argue that the public has a right to know whether the event will create financial obligations for the State, regardless of whether it is being presented as a privately sponsored undertaking.

The petition also raises broader questions about the financing and construction costs of Talanta Stadium, which is being prepared to host major sporting events.

It references previous parliamentary scrutiny of the project’s construction costs, which reportedly rose from an initial estimate of KSh35 billion to KSh45.85 billion.

The petitioners also point to concerns raised by the Auditor-General regarding contingent liabilities and infrastructure asset-backed security arrangements.

They argue that the stadium’s financing history makes transparency around the proposed opening event particularly important, especially where government resources or financial guarantees may be involved.

The petitioners further cite competing national priorities, including unemployment, gaps in healthcare, road infrastructure challenges and education funding, as reasons why public expenditure must be subjected to strict accountability.

The case places the proposed Bayern Munich-Ajax fixture under scrutiny over the extent of public involvement in an event the government has described as commercially self-sustaining.

The High Court is being asked to intervene to safeguard public resources and compel disclosure of the financial arrangements before any public funds or resources are committed to the match.

title: FIT KING Highlights Inclusive Sports Through Sponsorship of the 2026 San Diego Triathlon Challenge
article_text:
The brand's Gold Sponsorship supported a CAF event that brings attention to the opportunities and practical resources needed for participation in sport.

NEW YORK, Nov. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FIT KING joined the Challenged Athletes Foundation (CAF) as a Gold Sponsor of the 2026 San Diego Triathlon Challenge (SDTC), held in La Jolla on Oct. 25. The event brought attention to a simple but important reality: taking part in sport can depend on access to equipment, instruction and a supportive community as much as on individual motivation.

CAF works with individuals with physical disabilities to help expand opportunities in fitness and competitive athletics. Its grants and programs address needs that can make participation difficult, from adaptive equipment to training and competition-related resources. SDTC gives the public a visible window into that year-round work.

Sports participation is not a single experience. One person may be training for a competitive race, another may be returning to an activity after a long absence, and another may be joining a community event for the first time. Equipment needs, transportation, coaching and the availability of accessible activities can shape each person's options.

Adaptive sports equipment, including specialized cycles and prosthetic running equipment, can involve substantial costs. Access to qualified instruction and opportunities to practice also matters. CAF helps address these barriers through its grants and programs.

The 2026 SDTC program was adjusted after the swim portion was canceled, with the main competition proceeding in a run-bike-run format. The broader weekend included other opportunities for athletes and supporters to participate. The range of activities reinforced a defining feature of the event: people can belong to the same sports community without sharing the same course, ability or competitive goal.

For families, volunteers and supporters, the event also created opportunities to engage with adaptive sports beyond watching a finish line. That wider community context is part of what makes SDTC more than an ordinary product showcase or a single-day competition.

FIT KING participated as a Gold Sponsor and presented its FT-115A and FT-116A pneumatic compression massage boots at the expo. The two models are designed for at-home leg massage and relaxation, with selectable compression zones and adjustable settings. Product education was one part of the brand's event presence, separate from CAF's athlete support and grantmaking.

title: LHFX Formula 3 Partnership Backs Reza Seewooruthun in 2027
article_text:
LHFX has become Headline Partner to British racing driver Reza Seewooruthun for his debut season in the 2027 FIA Formula 3 Championship with Rodin Motorsport. The agreement marks the online forex and CFD broker’s first sports sponsorship, with its branding already appearing on Seewooruthun’s car during testing.

The agreement supports Seewooruthun as he moves from the Formula Regional European Championship into the next stage of international single-seater racing. He will remain with Rodin Motorsport, continuing a relationship developed during his 2026 Formula Regional campaign.

The partnership covers Seewooruthun’s preparations, testing and full 2027 F3 season. The LHFX name will feature on his car and race suit throughout the campaign.

“We’re delighted to be backing Reza as he steps up to Formula 3 with Rodin Motorsport. This is LHFX’s first sports sponsorship, and we’re proud to support him at such an important point in his career. We’re looking forward to cheering him on in 2027 and following his progress in Formula 3 and beyond.”

Seewooruthun’s move to F3 follows a progression through karting, junior car racing and single-seaters. He became English Junior Rotax Karting Champion in 2022 before completing a full Ginetta Junior campaign with R Racing in 2023. He finished third in that championship, recording four wins, seven podiums and three pole positions.

In 2024, he moved into single-seaters with Hitech Pulse-Eight Racing and finished third in the British F4 Championship. He subsequently stepped up to GB3 with Argenti with Prema in 2025, finishing fifth overall and taking his first victory in the series at the Hungaroring.

He joined Rodin Motorsport for the 2026 Formula Regional European Championship, recording two podium finishes. He will stay with Rodin as he learns the F3 car and prepares for his first season in the championship.

FIA Formula 3 sits below Formula 2 on the international single-seater ladder and races on selected Formula 1 weekends. Drivers compete in front of the Formula 1 paddock and fans attending the Grand Prix weekend.

The championship uses a common specification of car, making driver performance, preparation and the team’s work with the equipment central to the contest. For drivers moving up from regional championships, it is an opportunity to measure themselves against an international field while developing the skills needed for further progression.

Seewooruthun arrives with wins in junior categories and two Formula Regional podiums. His debut F3 season will put that experience to the test.

In his own announcement of the partnership, Seewooruthun described the commitment required from his family and supporters to build a racing career. He highlighted the role partners play in making test days, race weekends and moves into higher categories possible.

LHFX’s backing begins with testing and continues through Seewooruthun’s debut season. Fans will be able to follow his progress through the broker’s channels and his official website.

More information about the partnership is available on LHFX’s partnership page.

LHFX is an online forex and CFD broker offering access to forex, commodities, indices, stocks and cryptocurrency CFDs through MetaTrader 5. The business was founded by David Gladwin. Its Headline Partnership with Reza Seewooruthun is the company’s first sports sponsorship.

title: Danish badminton star fails to break curse as she loses eighth successive final
article_text:
There were bright spots in Kjaersfeldt’s performance, but at crucial moments, she struggled to match the Indian player’s high level.

After 39 minutes, she had to accept defeat, losing in straight sets with scores of 12-21, 14-21.

The Dane stayed within distance of Sindhu until 12-14 in the first set. From that point on, however, she lost her momentum, and Sindhu pulled away on the scoreboard by winning seven consecutive rallies.

Kjaersfeldt, ranked 25th in the world, kept her head held high and fought bravely in the second set against the world number eight.

She got off to a poor start in the set, falling behind 3-7. But she quickly fought back, winning three points in a row to close the gap.

Ultimately, however, the Dane lacked the necessary precision in her game. She struggled to hit the lines, often forcing her to play shots closer to the center of the court.

This made it too easy for Sindhu to handle, and she secured the victory in Germany in convincing fashion.

title: LIV Golf Champion Suffers Major Setback Amid Uncertain Future
article_text:
The future of LIV Golf remains uncertain, and several of the league’s players have now suffered another setback in their attempts to secure playing opportunities elsewhere.

Michael La Sasso, the 22-year-old golfer who won LIV Golf Indianapolis in August, failed to advance through the second stage of DP World Tour Q-School.

La Sasso wasn’t alone. Sam Horsfield, Yosuke Asaji and former LIV golfer Luis Masaveu also failed to qualify for the final stage, dealing a blow to their hopes of securing DP World Tour playing rights for 2027.

The results come as LIV players continue to explore alternatives amid uncertainty surrounding the league’s future.

While the eliminations do not necessarily leave the four players without playing opportunities next season, they have closed off one important route to securing a DP World Tour card.

La Sasso’s elimination is particularly notable given his breakthrough victory just over two months ago.

The former Ole Miss standout joined Phil Mickelson’s HyFlyers GC in January after winning the 2025 NCAA individual championship.

He struggled during much of his rookie campaign before delivering an impressive performance at LIV Golf Indianapolis on August 23.

La Sasso finished at 18-under par to defeat Jon Rahm by one stroke, becoming the youngest individual tournament winner in the league’s history.

However, that success did not carry over to DP World Tour qualifying.

La Sasso competed at Desert Springs Golf Club in Spain, where the top 20 finishers would advance to the final stage.

As Golf Monthly reported, he finished tied for 65th at five-under par, well outside the qualifying positions.

Yosuke Asaji also fell short at Desert Springs, finishing tied for 26th at 12-under.

Meanwhile, Horsfield finished tied for 52nd at Isla Canela Links, while Masaveu suffered a particularly disappointing elimination at Golf Las Pinaillas, losing in a playoff for the final qualifying spots.

The results arrive at a difficult time for players attempting to navigate uncertainty surrounding LIV Golf.

While LIV Golf has received some encouraging news lately, there are still huge questions about the league’s status in 2027.

As a result, several LIV players have been exploring potential arrangements that could provide playing opportunities on the DP World Tour in 2027.

The proposed arrangements reportedly involve players leaving LIV Golf and resolving their existing contractual obligations before receiving opportunities on the European circuit.

However, no such agreement has been confirmed for La Sasso or the other three golfers eliminated from Q-School.

The DP World Tour’s qualifying process provides another route for players attempting to secure their futures independently.

For La Sasso, the immediate future is not entirely without opportunities. The Sunshine Tour confirmed that he will compete in December’s AfrAsia Bank Mauritius Open on a tournament invitation.

Nevertheless, his failed Q-School campaign represents a disappointing development following the high of his LIV Golf triumph.

With the future of LIV still uncertain, La Sasso and several fellow players now face additional questions about their competitive schedules for 2027.
